caseno: Civil Revision No. 5754 of 2002
lawyer:
Mustafa Kamal Pasha, Advocate—For the Petitioners 
Md Ismail, Advocate—For the Opposite Parties
parties:
Abrara Begum and others ------ Petitioners 
vs 
Hosneara Begum & ors  ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Siddiqur Rahman Miah J: This revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of defendants-opposite parties petitioner Nos. 4 to 12 is directed against the impugned order No. 56 dated 4-9-2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong in Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 2000 under sections 114 and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure out of other Suit No. 207 of 1997 disposed of on 30-4-2000 by the learned Court of Subordinate Judge (now, Joint District Judge) 3rd Court, Chittagong.

2. The plaintiffs-petitioners-opposite parties Nos.1 to 5 filed a suit for declaration against the defendant Nos. 4 to 12 and others on 10-11-1997 with prayers for declaring the proceedings of certified case No. 2 of 1996-97 pending in the office of defendant No.1 fraudulent, collusive and void ab initio, for declaration of title in respect of the suit land and for correction of BS Khatian which is not binding upon the plaintiffs.

3. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that Rohini Ranjan Saha was the original owner in the suit property, that plaintiff's father Hafizur Rahman purchased the suit property on 28-7-1950 AD from Rohini Ranjan Saha through registered Saf kabala deed; that PS Khatain was prepared in the name of the plaintiff's father; that the plaintiffs' father Hafizur Rahman was an illiterate person; that Hafizur Rahman would love and believe his educated brother Nabidur Rahman very much; that Nabidur Rahman used to keep all deeds in his custody and would pay rent; that Hafizur Rahman died before BS field operation leaving minor son and daughters and that Nabidur Rahman assured that BS Khatian has been duly prepared on behalf of Hafizur Rahman's heirs and that plaintiffs did not take care as such. It is further stated that after the death of Nabidur Rahman, plaintiff No. 5 on behalf of all plaintiffs claimed all the deeds including the deed of suit property from the defendants Nos. 4 to 7 and then defendant No. 5 informed the plaintiffs that their claimed deeds have been lost and after collecting the certified copies of the deeds and khatians, it was found that BS khatian of the suit land has been wrongly prepared in the name of Nabidur Rahman instead of plaintiffs father and that plaintiff No.5 went to the office of the defendant No. 1 on 15-10-1997 for correction of BS khatian and came to know that defendant No. 1's office has no jurisdiction for correction and moreover, it was found that certificate case No. 2 of 1996-97 has been filed against Nabidur Rahman; that the said certificate case was collusive and malafide and therefore, the plaintiffs have been constrained to file the instant suit against the defendants on 10-11-1997.

4. Defendant Nos. 1 to 3 contested the suit by filing joint written statement denying all the material allegations of the plaint contending, inter alia, that the plaintiffs have no locus standi to file the present suit challenging the Certificate Case No. 2 of 1996-97 which is barred by section 37 of the Public Demands Recovery Act and section 42 of the Specific Relief Act; that the suit is not maintainable in the present form having no cause of action and that the suit is barred by limitation which is liable to be dismissed with cost.

5. The defendants Nos. 1 to 12 filed an application under rule 11, Order VII of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejecting the plaint alleging that the suit is barred by law.

6. The learned trial Court on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and relevant documents and other materials on record rejected the plaint by his order dated 30-4-2000 on the ground that as certificate case is pending Civil Court has no jurisdiction to declare the proceedings of the certificate case as illegal and malafide.

7. The plaintiffs opposite parties Nos. 4 to 12 preferred Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 2000 for setting aside the order of rejection on 30-4-2000 and the learned Joint District Judge, on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and materials on record, allowed the review Miscellaneous case setting aside the order of rejection.

8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order No. 56 dated 4-9-2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge in Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 2000 arising out of Other Suit No. 207 of 1997 disposed of on 30-4-2000, the plaintiff moved this Court and obtained the Rule.

9. The opposite parties Nos. 1 to 3 filed a counter-affidavit denying the petitioner's case, inter alia, contending that Hafizur Rahman, the predecessor of the plaintiffs-opposite parties Nos.1 to 5, purchased the suit land from one Rohini Ranjan Saha by executing kabala No. 467 dated 20-7-1950 and thereafter, got delivery of possession; that he mutated his name in PS khatian and had been in peaceful possession by paying rent to the appropriate authority during his lifetime, that Hafizur Rahman entrusted his brother and handed the relevant documents relating to landed property to his younger brother and that during BS operation Nabidur Rahman in collusion with the survey staff recorded his name in BS khatian No. 33 in respect of the suit land. It is further stated that heirs of Nabidur Rahman defendants-petitioners Nos.1 to 9 had been trying to dispossess the plaintiffs-opposite parties Nos. 1 to 5 from the suit land claiming their title on the basis of BS khatian.

10. It is further stated that the certificate case No.2 of 1996-97 is collusive and fraudulent, that the opposite parties Nos. 1 to 5 who are heirs of Hafizur Rahman, as plaintiffs were compelled to file Other Suit No. 207 of 1997 praying for declaration that certificate case No. 02 of 1996-97 is fraudulent and collusive; that the BS khatian No.33 was collusively made in the name of Nabidur Rahman and that for declaration of title in the suit land in favour of the heirs of plaintiff.

11. The defendant Nos. 1 to 9 as heirs of Nabidur Rahman filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for rejection of the plaint of Other Suit No. 207 of 1997 and the learned trial Court allowed the application rejecting the plaint of the suit by his order dated 30-4-2000. It is further stated that the plaintiff-opposite parties Nos. 1 to 5 as petitioners filed review petition under section 114 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure being Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 2000. The learned trial Court upon consideration of facts and circumstances of the case passed the order No. 56 dated 4-9-2002 which is under challenge.

12. Now, the point for determination is whether the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong committed an error of law resulting in an error in his decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the order dated 4-9-2002.

13. Mr Mostafa Kamal Pasha, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that since Certificate Case No. 2 of 1996-97 is pending regarding the self-same suit land, plaintiffs-opposite parties' suit as well as the Miscellaneous case under sections 114 and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is barred by section 37 of the Public Demands Recovery Act, plaintiffs-opposite parties Nos.1 to 5 have no cause of action for reviewing the order; that the suit is barred by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and Order II, rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure; that the learned Court below has no inherent power under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure to review the decree which was perfectly valid and the impugned order No. 56 dated 4-9-2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge is based on conjecture and surmise which is liable to be set aside.

14. The learned Advocate for the petitioners cited the decision in the case of Nurul Hussain vs Government of People's Republic of Bangladesh reported in 49 DLR (AD) 108 and in the case of Basharatullah being dead his heirs Fazle Karim and others vs Government of Bangladesh and others reported in 1996 BLD (AD) 9.

15. Mr Md Ismail, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties, submits that the learned trial Court most legally and judiciously on proper consideration of the facts as well as law involved in the declaration suit, allowed the said review petition in accordance with law on finding that the claim of title, made by the plaintiff in the suit is to be decided on examination and consideration of evidence to be adduced by the respective parties in their respective case. He further submits that the learned trial Court has committed no error of law resulting in an error in his decision occasioning failure of justice. He further submits that when an application for review is allowed by a competent Court, the aggrieved party may prefer an appeal challenging the order. But defendants Nos. 4 to 12 filed a revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure challenging the order No. 56 dated 4-9-2002 passed by the learned trial Court and their filing of a revisional application challenging the appellate order is without jurisdiction.

16. The learned Advocate for the plaintiffs-opposite parties cited the case of Mir Delwar Hossain, vs Mirza Joynal Abedin Moktar reported in 29 DLR 214, in the case of Alhaj Md Ruhul Amin vs Dhaka Municipal Corporation and others reported in 36 DLR 1; in the case of Maulvi Md Mazaharul Huq Chowdhury vs Nagendralal Dey and others reported in 9 DLR 456 and in the case of Hussain Bakhsh vs Settlement Commissioner and another reported in 21 DLR (SC) 456.

17. The point for determination is, whether the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong committed an error of law resulting in an error in his decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned order dated 4-9-2002 allowing the Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 2000 setting aside the decree rejecting the plaint.

18. The main contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioners is that suit as well as Miscellaneous case under sections 114 and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is barred by section 37 of the Public Demands Recovery Act.

19. The order dated 30-4-2000 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong is without jurisdiction because of the pendency of certificates proceeding, and the Civil Court has every jurisdiction to give any verdict on the suit. The contention of the learned Advocate for the defendant-opposite parties referring the case of Moulvi Md Mazaharul Huq Chowdhury vs Nagendralal Dey and others reported in 9 DLR 456 wherein their Lordships decided that section 37 of Public Demands Recovery Act is not bar to a suit in a civil Court where the proceedings under the Act are wholly authorised and fraudulent. In the instant case there is an allegation of fraud as regard the certificate case and such allegation of fraud has given the civil Court a jurisdiction to look into the matter. Where the action of the revenue authorities abuses the provisions of the Public Demands Recovery Act, section 37 of the Act does not oust the jurisdiction of the Civil Court to make a declaration, to issue injunction otherwise to grant adequate relief. The proviso to section 37 of the said Act itself recognises the principle that a suit on the allegations of fraud stands on a totally different footing altogether.

20. Further contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner is that the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong had no power to review the order. The learned Advocate for the plaintiffs-opposite parties on this point referred the decision in the case of Alhaj Md Ruhul Amin vs Dhaka City Corporation and others wherein his Lordship decided, that it is well settled that the right of review of a judgment is a substantive right and the scope, extent, manner and forum of review are circumscribed by the provisions of the statute which confer on the litigants the right of review. When error on the face of the decree is found it will lie also to the successor of the judge who passed the order. Review on such ground is entertainable. In the instant case when the error was apparent on the face of the record, the learned Joint District Judge had every jurisdiction to review the decree and the learned Joint District Judge rightly did it.

21. The learned Advocate for the opposite parties further referred the decision in the case of Hussain Bakhsh vs Settlement Commissioner and another reported in 21 DLR 456 wherein our Appellate Division opined that the right to claim review of any decision of a court of law, like the right to appeal is a substantive right and not a mere matter of procedure. This is equally true in a case of review, because both appeal and review though they differ in scope are substantive rights. The learned Joint District Judge had right to review the order and he very judiciously did so in passing the impugned order and setting aside the decree and the order of rejection of plaint.

<u>22. In legal parlance review is a judicial reexamination of the case by the Judge, in certain circumstance. Section 114 of the Code gives us substantive right of review in certain circumstance and Order XLVII provides therefore. Any person aggrieved by a decree or order may apply for a review of judgment where no appeal is allowed or where an appeal is allowed but no appeal has been filed against such decree or order. A person aggrieved means a person who has suffered a legal grievance or against whom a decision has been pronounced which has wrongfully deprived him of something or wrongfully refused him something or wrongfully affected his title to something.</u>

<u>23. A power of review should not be confused with appellate power which enables an appellate Court to correct all errors committed by a subordinate Court. A well settled principle of law is that a judgment pronounced by a competent Court must be accepted and implemented and departure therefrom is permissible only on fulfilment of certain conditions. It should not be forgotten that a review is not an appeal in disguise whereby an erroneous decision is reheard and corrected.</u>

<u>24. A review of a judgment is a serious step and reluctant resort to it is proper only where a glaring omission or patent mistake or like grave error has crept in earlier by judicial fallibility. A mere repetition through different counsels of old and over-ruled arguments cannot create a good ground for review. An application for review of a judgment may be made on any of the following grounds: discovery of new and important matter or evidence or mistake or error apparent on the face of the record or any other sufficient reasons.</u>

<u>25. In view of the above discussion, we find that the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong by his order dated 30-4-2000 committed no wrong in rejecting the plaint. Since there is allegation of fraud, in such case the Civil Court has every jurisdiction to try the case and thus section 37 of Public Demands Recovery Act provides that case may be brought in the civil Court in respect of any such question upon the ground of fraud is involved in the suit. In view of our discussion made above, we are of the view that the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong did not commit any error of law resulting in an error in passing the impugned order dated 4-9-2002. Therefore, we find no merit in this Rule.</u>

26. In the result the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost and the order No. 56 dated 4-9-2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong in Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 2002 under sections 114 and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure arising out of Other Suit No. 207 of 1997 disposed of on 30-4-2000 by the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong. The suit will proceed as usual in accordance with law. The learned Joint District Judge is directed to dispose of the suit expeditiously preferably within 4(four) months from the date of receipt of this order.

Communicate at once.

End.

caseno: Civil Appeal No. 91 of 2003
lawyer:
Mahbuhey Alam, Senior Advocate with Mr. M. K. Rahman, Advocate, instructed by Chowdhury Md. Zahangir, Advocate -on-Record ----- For the Petitioners 
A. K. Badrul Huq, Senior Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate on record ----- For respondents

Most. Monowara Begum and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Malanch Bibi and others ----- Respondents
case_source: (From the Judgment and Order dated 3rd June, 2001 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2516 of 1996 with Civil Rule No. 350(R) of 1996)
full_judgment:
S. K. Sinha J:- This appeal by leave granted by this Court from the judgment and order dated 31st May, 2001 and 3rd June 2001 of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2516 of 1996 making the rule absolute by reversing those dated 27th May, 1996 of the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Barisal in Title Appeal No. 158 of 1980 who affirmed those dated 16th June, 1980 of the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Barisal in Title Suit No. 33 of 1960. 

2. Appellant instituted the suit for declaration of title to the suit lands and further declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 730 of 1962 to be void, fraudulent and not binding upon him.

3. Appellant's case in short is that the Original maliks of the holding Mini and his wife Sarola left this Country for India in 1962 and the suit holding measuring an area of 1.72 acres of land was sold in auction for arrear of rents. The plaintiff auction purchased the same on 22nd October, 1962 in 3 (three) certificate cases and got delivery of possession on 4th December, 1962. The record of right was however not prepared in the name of the plaintiff and it was recorded in the name of defendant on the basis of an exparte decree passed in Title Suit No. 730 of 1962, which clouded his title in the suit lands. 

4. Defendant contested the suit contending inter alia that he got settlement of the suit lands in Baishak 1350 B.S. corresponding to 1943 A.D. from Nalini and Sarola on the basis of dakhilas and has since been possessing thereon. The defendant denied the plaintiffs title and claimed that the plaintiff did not acquire any title on the basis of certificate sale and he was not given possession of the suit property.

5. The trial Court on consideration of the evidence on record held that the sale was a nullity; the plaintiff acquired no right in the suit lands on the basis of auction purchase and that he was not in possession of the suit property. The lower appellate Court affirmed the 'finding of the trial Court. The plaintiff took a Second Appeal being Second Appeal No. 1114 of 1967 which was also dismissed. Thereafter the plaintiff-appellant preferred Civil Appeal No. 26 of 1975 before this Court. This Court observed that the plaintiff had acquired a valid title in the suit lands by way of auction purchase, and the defendant could not challenge by way of defence the validity of the certificate sale on the ground of non-service of notice under section 7 of the Public Demands Recovery Act, that the findings of the Courts below that the defendant had failed to establish his settlement from Nalini and Sarola was correct and that the exparte decree passed in Title Suit No. 730 of 1962 was also fraudulent and void. With these findings the Appellate Division set aside the judgments of the Courts below in part and sent back the suit on remand to the trial Court for allowing the plaintiff to amend his pleadings by adding the. prayer for recovery of possession on payment of proper court fee with a direction that the trial Court shall decide the question of recovery of possession by the plaintiff and the ancillary question of adverse possession of the defendant, if, so raised and also to afford the defendant to file additional written statement. The Appellate Division also allowed the parties, if they prayed, to adduce additional evidence and the court thought fit to allow. 

6. After the remand the plaintiff amended the plaint and the defendant also filed an additional written statement. The plaintiff thereupon re-examined Golam Hafiz.Miah (PW.1) and also examined 3 other witnesses in support of recovery of possession. The defendant also examined 3 witnesses in support of his claim of adverse possession. The learned Subordinate Judge thereupon by judgment and order dated 16th June, 1982 decreed the suit declaring plaintiffs title in 'Kha' schedule lands and also declared the exparte decree passed in Title Suit No. 732 of 1962 as fraudulent, void and not binding upon the plaintiff. The trial Court also decreed the suit for recovery of khas possession of the suit lands on removal on the structures thereon. On appeal by the defendant, the Court of appeal below by judgment and order dated 27th May, 1996 affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court. The defendant thereupon moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2516 of 1996 and a Single Bench of the High Court Division by judgment and order dated 31st May 2001 and 3rd June, 2001 made- the rule absolute and set aside those of the Courts below and dismissed the suit. 

7. It was urged on behalf of the plaintiff-appellant that the High Court Division acted illegally in interfering with the con-current findings of fact arrived at by the Courts below that the defendant raised the constructions in 1967 by dispossessing the plaintiff, that the plaintiff got possession of the suit lands after auction purchase, that the defendant's failed to prove the settlement of the suit lands and that the defendant fraudulently obtained the exparte decree in title suit no. 730 of 1962. Learned Counsel has referred the cases of Shambhu Nath Poddar Vs. Bangladesh Railway and others 43 DLR (AD) 82, Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary Ministry of Works Vs. Chand Mia and others 44 DLR (AD) 98 Shamser Ali (Md.) and others. Vs. Mosammat Kafizan Bibi, 44 DLR (Al)) 231 and Hussain Ahmed Chowdhury @ Ahmed Hossain Chowdhury and others Vs. Md. Nurul Amin and others 47 DLR (Al)) 162. 

8. The High Court Division while reversing the concurrent findings of the Courts below reassessed the evidence on record as if it were hearing a first appeal. The High Court Division observed that the plaintiff examined P.Ws. 6, 7 and 8 with-out permission of the trial Court and that the claim of the plaintiff that he was dis-possessed by the defendant on the first part of 1967 was not a believable story, This finding of examination of witnesses without permission of the Court is base-less, inasmuch as, unless the parties prayed for examination of the witnesses, how the trial Court allowed each of the parties- to examine 3 witnesses? The examination of witnesses presupposed that on the prayers of the parties, both the parties examined witnesses in support of their respective claims the High Court Division observed that the plaintiff came out with a new cause of action without disclosing about the exact date of dispossession and that the Courts below also did not consider some material evidence of D.Ws. 5, 6, and 7 and therefore, the judgment of the Court of appeal below is defective as it being based upon misreading and non-consideration of the material evidence on record. As regards the observation of non-consideration of the evidence of D.Ws. 5-7, we find that the learned judge of the High Court Division has not properly appreciated the Judgment of the Courts below. Learned Judge did not point out whose evidence the lower appeal Court misread and non -considered .The Courts below on proper appreciating the evidence on record arrived at the finding that the defendant dispossessed the plaintiff during the pendency of the suit. This finding is Vague and indefinite.

9. In the application for amendment of the plaint the plaintiff claimed that after filing the appeal in the lower appellate Court the defendant having realized that he would not get relief in the suit with a view to forestall the appeal raised some constructions in the suit lands taking advantage of the plaintiffs temporary absence in the suit lands in the first part of 1967 and dis-possessed him. The trial Court on assessment of the evidence on record came to a positive finding that the plaintiff acquired title of the suit lands on the basis of auction purchase on 21st September, 1962 that he got delivery of possession on 4th December, 1962, and that the defendant had no possession before, 1962 and he had raised constructions during the pendency of the suit. 

10. In view of the averments made in paragraph 9 of the written statement filed on 4th June, 1964 that the defendant converted the suit lands into null lands after taking settlement in 1350 B.S., the Court of appeal below disbelieved the defendant's claim of possession and observed that this statement of the defendant proved that he did not raise construction in the suit lands after taking settlement. The Court of appeal below noticed that after the amendment of the plaint, the defendant filed an additional written statement on 12th August, 1977 and in paragraph 4 he stated that after the disposal of the suit on 12th September, 1966 he spent over Tk. 50,000/- and constructed a semi pucca house with corrugated sheets on the suit lands and in the western bite he constructed another permanent structure by spending over Tk. 40.,000/- and some other permanent structures , sanitary latrine and road at a cost of Tk. 65,000/-. In view of these claim of the defendant, the appellate Court came to the conclusion that the defendant raised the constructions after the disposal of the suit. In arriving as such conclusion the Court of appeal below also noticed a statement of Khadem Ali (D.W.5) who did not say anything about the construction in the suit lands in his earlier statement but after recall on 20th March, 1980, he stated that the defendant raised construction in 1372 B.S. by spending of Tk. about 3,00,000/-. The lower appellate Court came to a definite finding that the defendant made the constructions during the pendency of the suit and dispossessed the plaintiff. 

11. The Court of appeal below also on consideration of the evidence of Golam Hafiz (P.W.1), Mofizuddin Sarder (P.W.2), Ashraf Ali Sarder (P.W.3) and Mohammad Ali (P.W.4) and the documentary evidence filed by the plaintiff held that the plaintiff got possession of the suit lands after auction purchase and that he was dispossessed by the defendant in 1967. The Court of appeal below further observed that the defendant failed to prove that he took settlement of the suit lands from Sarala Sundari and Nalini and that the exparte decree obtained in Title Suit No. 730 of 1962 was fraudulent and collusive and not binding upon the plaintiff. These findings of the Court of appeal below are based upon proper appreciation of the evidence on record and these findings of fact can not be disturbed by the High Court Division in exercise of revisional jurisdiction in the absence of misreading or non-consideration of the material evidence in arriving at such findings. The learned Judge of the High Court Division totally ignoring that he was hearing the revision petition against the concurrent findings of fact reassessed the evidence and interfered with the concurrent findings of fact. 

12. The exercise of revisional jurisdiction is confined to question of jurisdiction. While in a first appeal the Court is free to decide all questions of law and fact which arise in the suit; in exercise of its revision-al jurisdiction the High Court Division is not entitled to reexamine or reassess the evidence on record and substitute its own findings on facts for those of the subordinate Courts. Jurisdiction means "the entitlement to enter upon the enquiry in question." The word is a verbal cast of many colors. The jurisdiction of the High Court Division in revision is a limited one. The section is not directed against conclusions of law or fact in which the question of jurisdiction is not involved. Section 115 empowers to satisfy the High Court Division on matters that (a) the order of the Subordinate Court is within its jurisdiction (b) the case is one in which the Court ought to exercise jurisdiction, and (c) in exercise of jurisdiction the Court has not acted illegally, that is, in breach of some provisions of law, or with material irregularity by committing some error of procedure in Course of the trial which is material in that it may have affected the ultimate decision. 

13. In the case of Shambhu Nath Poddar, this Court observed that the revisional court acted beyond its' jurisdiction in setting aside the concurrent finding of fact, when there is no misreading and mis-appreciation of the evidence on record. In the case of Chand Mia, this Court held "The lower appellate Court had given a finding that there was no service of summons upon the appellant in that suit. It was no function of the High Court Division to sit in appeal over that finding of the lower appellate Court in the revisional jurisdiction." In the case of Hussain Ahmed Chowdhury it was observed that if there is misreading or non- consideration of material evidence then the High Court Division was within its competence to dispose of the matter on the materials on record. 

14. Learned Counsel appearing for the defendant-respondent failed to point out any misreading or non-consideration of the evidence on record by the Courts below in arriving at those findings of fact. It is argued that in the earlier judgment the trial Court had clearly observed that the plaintiff was out of possession till 1966 and this finding was affirmed by the High Court Division in the second appeal, and this concurrent finding having not reversed by the Appellate Division is binding upon the plaintiff. It is further argued that the amendment of the plaint is barred by limitation. According to the Learned counsel, since the suit is for possession followed by dispossession, Article 142 of the Limitation Act is attracted and the plaintiff having failed to prove that he was dispossessed after the institution of the suit, the prayer for amendment of the plaint is barred by limitation. In support of his contention he has referred the cases of Abdul Wadud and others vs. Abdul Wahed and others, 14 MLR(AD)106, Ahmed Miaji and others Vs. Eakub All Munshi and others 12 DLR 708 and Munshi Dudhu Mia and others Vs Rahimuddin and others 16 DLR 56. 

15. We find no force in the submissions of the learned counsel in view of the findings of the Appellate Division that "the plaintiff purchaser acquired a paramount title in the certificate sale. The certificate sale under Sub-Section,(3), we have already observed, corresponds to rent decree in some cases, and the purchaser acquired in absolute right in the holding, except the protected interest described in the proviso to the sub-section (3), but with the right to annual the incumbrances in the manner prescribed under the Act. We are not concerned with any protected interest here. The defendant, no doubt, claimed an under rayati right by virtue of settlement from Nalini and his wife, the certificate debtors, but his claim is not succeeded .
" The Appellate Division further observed that "the certificate debtors being the sole tenants, and the plaintiff the sole purchaser of the certificate sale, he, under S.20(1) of the Act acquired no right, title and interest of the certificate debtors, and in the present ease the entire interest of the holding in question, and the holdings so passed in the plaintiff under section 20(3) with right to annual the encumbrances and that the true import of the Section (S.36) is that the sale in a certificate proceeding for non-service of notice under section 7 is valid against whole world for all times, and as against the certificate debtor, after a period of one year, from the date of delivery of property to the purchaser, if no proceeding for setting aside the sale has been started in the mean while." 

16. The submission that the amendment of the plaint is barred by limitation is based on misconception of law, inasmuch as, it is now settled that as to the question of limitation there are two ways in which the same may arise. "First, whether the claim to be included was barred on the date of the institution of the suit. Secondly, whether the claim is barred on the date of the prayer for amendment. On the first case, the prayer for amendment can not be allowed as it is barred on the date of institution of the suit and on the second case, the prayer can be allowed." Reference in this connection is the case of Nurun Nahar V. Mohd. Fazlur Rahman (1979) BSCR 135. In this case the question of limitation does not arise since both the Courts below have concurrently found that the defendant has dispossessed the plaintiff during the pendency of the suit. The suit was instituted on 7th March; 1964 and though the amendment of the plaint was made on 19th April, 1977, as soon as the prayer for amendment was allowed, the said amendment related back to the date of institution of the suit, as if those statements in the amendment petition were made in the original plaint. In that view of the matter, the learned Counsel is absolutely wrong in his contention that the amendment is barred by limitation. 

17. In the case of Ahmed Miaji referred by the learned counsel, it was observed that "the plaintiffs have set up a case of possession followed by dispossession. They must prove possession within 12 years of the suit. Plaintiffs have failed to prove their case." In the case of Munshi Dudhu Mia, it was observed that "Article 142 of the Limitation Act applies when a plaintiff set up a case of possession followed by dispossession. In such a case the onus is on the plaintiff to prove that he was in possession within 12 years from the date of the institution of the suit." We do not dispute the observations made in the above cases. We fail to understand why the learned counsel has referred those decisions in view of the concurrent findings of the Courts below on the point of possession and dispossession. In the case of Abdul Wadud referred by the learned Counsel, the facts are as follows: in the appellate Court the plaintiffs filed an application for amendment of the plaint stating inter alia that the defendants no. 9-12 dispossessed them from part of the suit lands during the pendency of the suit. The appellate Court rejected the application on the reasoning that in the application the plaintiffs did not give specific date or month or any specific description of the incident to the alleged dispossession and that the application for amendment was barred by limitation. This finding has been affirmed by the High Court Division and the Appellate Division maintained the order of the High Court Division. In the facts of the given case, this decision has no manner of application in view of the discussions made earlier. 

18. The High Court Division laded to Appellate Division Cases notice that there are limited campus to be resolved in this matter by the Courts below in view of the points formulated by the Appellate Division for decision to the effect that the plaintiff be afforded an opportunity "to amend his pleading by adding the prayer for recovery of possession on payment of proper court fee. The Court shall decide the question of the recovery of possession by the plaintiff, and the ancillary question of adverse possession of the defendant, if, so raised." 

19. The Courts below accordingly decided the issue in favour of the plaintiff on assessment of the evidence on record, and disbelieved the defendant's claim of adverse possession on a clear finding that he had failed to substantiate his plea of adverse possession. The High Court Division has exceeded its jurisdiction in interfering with the judgments of the courts below 

20. The appeal is therefore allowed. The judgment of the High Court Division is set aside and restored those of the Courts below.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 491 of 2009
lawyer:

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 15.12.2008 passed by ''the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.1675 of 1994.)
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J. This Civil; Petition for leave to appeal has been directed against the judgment and order dated 15.12.2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.1675 of 1994 making the Rule absolute by setting aside the judgment and decree dated 02.04.1994 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Chittagong in Other Appeal No.283 of 1991 allowing the appeal in pan and modifying the judgment and decree dated 26.05.1991 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Satkania, Chittagong in Other Suit No.150 of 1986 decreeing the suit.

<u>2. The predecessors of the present petitioners, as plaintiffs, instituted Other Suit No.150 of 1986 before the Court of Assistant Judge, Satkania against the present respondents for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and also for perpetual injunction in respect of 1.3875 acres of land out of 1.85 acres in 12 annas share which was fully described in the; schedule to the plaint. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that the property in schedule to the plaint is a tank and the bank surrounding it which is popularly known as "Butter Pukur". That in the Moghi Chitta Survey the schedule property was recorded as Taraf Syed Mohammad Arshad Kishmat Malik Rahman. That the owner of the Taraf being a resident of distant place never possessed the same and the same was under adverse possession of Abdul Aziz son of Hamid Baksha and Abdul Fattah son of Munshi Ali Baksha for more than the statutory period of limitation. That during C.S. operation the Government enlisted the suit land as Nayabad Mohal and as per possession of Abdul Aziz and Abdul Fattah recorded their names under Jote No.5. That Abdul Aziz and Abdul Fattah possessed the tank for more than 90 years by payment of rents to the Government. That the said tank became silted up and Abdul Aziz and others settled the same to Mofzulur Rahman, Abdul Gafur, Abdul Bari and Ali Hossain the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 32-62. That Mofzulur and others having been in possession of the said tank re-excavated the same at huge cost and on behalf of the settlement holders their elder brother Ali Hossain received the receipt from the labourers for re-excavation of the tank. That Ali Hossain was literate person and acted as "Karjakark" on behalf of all family members. That in R.S. record of rights the tank was recorded in the names of Abdul Rajjak and others sons of Abdul Aziz and Faruk Ahmed and others-sons of Abdul Fattah with a note of permissive possession of Ali Hossain and others. That the surveyors and employees inadvertently recorded such wrong note of permissive possession of Ali Hossain and others instead of recording their names as tenants in corfa right. That after promulgation of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1951 the predecessors of the plaintiffs became the raiyats under the Government and the plaintiffs have been possessing the said tank on payment of rents. That upon an application made by the predecessor of the defendant No. 32 under Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, a proceeding under Section 145 of the said Code being Miscellaneous Case No. 8 of 1949 was started in respect of the suit property and in that case the learned Magistrate found right and title of Golam Sultan and others sons of Ali Hossain and put them in possession of the suit property. That thereafter the predecessor of the plaintiffs had been possessing the suit tank by rearing and preserving fish therein and by planting trees on the bank of the tank within the knowledge of the defendants. That the plaintiffs had no good relation with the proforma defendant Nos. 32-62 the descendants of Ali Hossain and as such they have been made proforma defendants in the suit. That the principal defendants have no right, title, interest and possession in the suit tank, but they gave out in the locality that the suit tank was taluki property of Azmatullah and Muzibullah and  that the same was purchased by Ezzad Ali and others in auction and subsequently the predecessor of the defendants took settlement of the suit tank from them. That the principal defendants, who are rich men, have been making plan to forcibly enter into the suit tank, take away the trees therefrom and construct house thereon and thus the plaintiffs have been constrained to file the suit for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and for permanent injunction in respect of 12 annas shares in the schedule property.</u>

3. The predecessors of the present respondent Nos. 1-19 as defendant Nos. 1-4 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement. These defendants denied the material case of the plaintiffs and stated, inter-alia, that the suit is not maintainable as it is barred by principle of res-judicata. The positive case of the defendant Nos.1- 4, in short, is that the suit property which is known as "Burrer Pukur" was recorded in Moghi Chita Survey as Plot No.699 under Taraf Syed Md. Arshad. That Azmatullah and Mujibullah became the tenants under Taraf through settlement. That for arrear rent the suit property was put into auction and Ijjat Ali, Mosharrof Ali and Anwar Ali purchased the same in auction and got possession thereof. That the said auction purchasers subsequently settled this property to Ali Mahmud on 25th falgun, 1257 B.S. Ali Mahmud possessed the suit tank by rearing and preserving fish and the bank by planting and collecting usufructs thereof. Thereafter Ali Mahmud died leaving behind two sons namely Abdul Ali and Nazir Ali. On 22.07.1280 B.S. Nazir Ali transferred his share in favour of Abdul Ali by registered kabala and in the said kabala Ali Hossain the predecessors of the plaintiffs was an attesting witness. That Abdul Ali became sole owner of the suit tank and constructed house on the bank of the tank. That the landlord collected rent from Abdul Ali and others through Rent Suit Nos.765 of 1914 and 1397 of 1918. That meanwhile the suit tank was recorded in plot Nos.611 and 612 in the names of Abdul Aziz and Abdul Fattah in the cadastral survey. That such record was wrong and baseless. That the Government acquired no right or title in the suit land and it was never taken as khas land of the Government. That the tank was never included in Nayabad Mahal. That Abdul Aziz and Abdul Fattah never possessed the suit tank. That preparation of the R.S. record of rights following the C.S. record of right in the names of Abdul Aziz and others was equally wrong and never acted upon. That the predecessors of the plaintiffs and proforma defendant Nos. 32 62 created and fabricated the so called unregistered patta dated 10.05.1913. "That the said so called patta is seen to be written after 21/22 years of purchase of the stamps. That the predecessor of the plaintiffs claimed the suit land as their purchased land in Other Suit No.17 of 1957, but failed to produce any kabala and never pointed out the existence of patio dated 10.05.1913. That at the time of R.S. operation the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1-4 Abdul Ali went to Rengun for earning money and he entrusted his brother-in-law Ali .Hossain-the predecessors of the plaintiffs to get the tank recorded in his name, but Ali Hossain got the tank fraudulently recorded in the names of Syed Abdul Aziz and others with a note of permissive possession of Ali Hossain. That after returning from Rengoon Abdul Ali died leaving behind defendant No.1 and Jobbar Ali as two sons and two daughters. That the defendant No.1 and his brother Jobbar Ali and sister Amena Khaton instituted Other Suit No. 17 of 1957 and obtained a decree declaring their title in the suit tank. That thereafter defendant Nos. 1-14 and 15 of the said suit filed two different appeals being Nos. 498 of 1958 and 27 of 1959 before the District Ridge which were dismissed on contest and thereafter Second appeal being No. 505 of 1963 was filed before the High Court Division which also was dismissed. That the plaintiffs never had any title or possession in the suit tank and as such the suit filed by them is liable to be dismissed.

4. Both the parties adduced evidence, both oral and documentary, in support of their  respective cases before the trial court. On consideration of those evidence the trial court found that the plaintiffs proved their title and possession in the 12 annas share in the suit tank and also found that the suit was not barred by Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure since the plaintiffs or their predecessors were not party in Title Suit No.17 of 1957. The trial court, therefore, decreed the suit declaring title of the plaintiffs in 12 annas share in the suit tank, confirming their possession therein and also restraining the principal defendants from entering into the suit tank. Against that judgment and order of the trial court the contesting defendants preferred appeal. The appellate court also found that the plaintiffs had right, title and possession in 12 annas share in the suit tank; but the appellate court opined that the plaintiffs were not entitled to any decree of perpetual injunction against the defendants as they admitted possession of the defendants in the rest four annas share in the suit tank. The appellate court, therefore, allowed the appeal in part setting aside the decree of perpetual injunction and affirming the decree declaring the plaintiffs title in 12 annas share in the suit tank and confirming their possession therein. The contesting defendants being aggrieved by that judgment and order of the appellate court filed the aforementioned Civil Revision No.1675 of 1994 before the High Court Division.

5. The High Court Division allowed the revisional application by making the rule absolute setting aside the judgment of both The courts below and dismissing the suit making observations that the plaintiffs alleged story of taking settlement of the suit tank by their predecessors by an unregistered patta of the year 1913 from Abdul Aziz and others had not been proved at all by any evidence. The revisional court disbelieved the plaintiffs' alleged possession in the suit tank on the basis of alleged patta making comment to the effect that none of the witnesses of the plaintiffs are at all competent to give evidence in support of alleged possession of the plaintiffs in the suit tank on the basis of alleged patta of the year 1913. The revisional court did not accept also the plaintiffs case of adverse possession making observation and comment to the effect that during trial of the suit no such issue was framed as to whether the plaintiffs acquired title in the suit tank on the basis of adverse possession and that no evidence also was led to that effect. The revisional court, however, did not accept contesting defendant's case that the suit was not maintainable as it was barred by principle of res-judicata pointing out that in the previous suit neither the plaintiffs nor any of their predecessors were made party.

6. We have heard Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, the learned Senior Advocate, for the petitioners and also Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Senior Advocate for the respondent Nos. 1-19.

<u>7. Assailing the impugned judgment of the High Court Division Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali has mainly argued that the High Court Division has erred in not believing the patta a more than 30 years old document as genuine for the reason that no competent witness came before court to prove this pasta without considering at all the fact that this patta being a very old document of the year 1913 AD none was available to give evidence in support of execution of this patta executed in the year 1913 AD; that the High Court Division did not take into consideration the fact also that though no person could be produced before the trial court to prove the genuineness of this patta but there were some other most dependable evidence which supported the genuineness of this patta, that the CS. khatian, R.S. khatian and also the rent receipts showing payment of rent by the plaintiffs and their predecessors supported the genuineness of this patta, but the revisional court did not take into consideration all these valuable documentary evidence at all.</u>

8. The learned Counsel for the petitioners has stated that the plaintiffs, in their plaint, categorically stated and made out a case of adverse possession also and in the prayer portion of the plaint also they prayed for declaration of their title in the suit property by virtue adverse possession and adduced sufficient evidence, both oral and documentary, in support of their possession in the suit property for more than 90 years and both the courts of fact, in consideration of these evidence, found the plaintiffs' right, title and possession in the suit property. The learned Counsel has argued that the revisional court without reversing this concurrent finding of both the courts of facts most erroneously held that the plaintiffs alleged adverse possession in the suit property could not he accepted as no issue to that effect was framed in the suit. The learned Advocate has contended that since there was specific pleading of adverse possession from the side of the plaintiff the revisional court should not have dismissed the suit for the reason only that no issue was framed by the trial court as to whether the plaintiffs acquired title on the basis of adverse possession, and that the revisional court, on such finding ought to have sent back the suit on remand to the trial court for disposal of the suit afresh after framing an issue as to plaintiffs claim of adverse possession.

9. The learned Counsel for the petitioners has argued also that the revisional court has committed wrong and also injustice in setting, aside the concurrent findings and decisions of the courts of facts without taking into consideration the broad fact that the contesting defendants could not prove their case by adducing necessary evidence.

10. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Counsel for the respondent Nos.1- 19 has made submission supporting the impugned judgment.

11. We have considered the submissions of the learned Counsels of both sides and gone through the impugned judgment and also the judgments of the Appellate Court and the trial court.

<u>12. Considering the facts and circumstances we find that this civil petition for leave to appeal merits consideration. In the circumstances leave is granted to consider the ground No.2 which is quoted below:-</u>

<u>"Because by way of patta C.S. and R.S. record was duly prepared in the names of the predecessors of the present   petitioners and have been in continuous possession since 90 years;  that on the basis of patta the plaintiff produced "Dakhila" in the trial court which was exhibited without objection that the defendants could not prove that the dakhila was illegal, forged or otherwise created; that the lower appellate court also affirmed the findings of the trial court, but the learned High Court Division without considering the same and out of misreading and misinterpretation of the evidences illegally made the Rule absolute holding that the patta was not genuine and as such the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be interfered with by this Hon'ble Court."</u>

13. Security of Tk. 1,000/- is to be deposited within 1 (one) month.

14. Preparation of paper book is dispensed with as prayed for.

15. Parties are directed to maintain status quo till disposal of the appeal.

End.

full_judgment:
A. B. M. Khairul Haque J:- These are petitions for leave to appeal arising out of the judgment and order dated 12.11.2008 discharging the Rules passed in Civil Revision No. 4612 of 2003 and the Civil Revision No. 925 of 2004. 

2. The petitioner Nos. 1 to 3 filed a suit being the Title Suit No. 301 of 1976 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Kushtia, against Mahtabuddin Biswas, the predecessor of the present respondents, praying for a declaration of title in the suit-land with a further declaration that the registered deed No. 6812 dated 12.10.1974, registered at the Kumarkhali Sub-Registry Office to be forged and not binding upon them. The defendant Mahtabuddin contested the suit by filing a written statement contending inter-alia that he is the owner of the property by virtue of a registered kabala Deed No. 6812 dated 12.10.1974 and that he is in possession since his such purchase. 

3. The aforesaid Mahtab also filed a suit being the Title Suit No. 11 of 1995 in the same Court against the plaintiffs of the aforesaid suit, praying for decree for declaration of his title in the suit land. 

4. Both the above Title Suit No.301 of 1976 and the Title Suit No. 11 of 1995 were heard' simultaneously. The learned Joint-District Judge dismissed the Title Suit No. 301 of 1976 and decreed the Title Suit No. 11 of 1995. As such, the petitioners preferred two appeals. Title Appeal No. 248 of 2002 was filed in respect of the decree of dismissal in the Title Suit No. 301 of 1976 and the Title Appeal No. 249 of 2002 were filed in respect of the decree passed in the Title Suit No. 11 of 1995. The learned District Judge, after hearing, decreed the Title Suit No. 301 of 1976 and dismissed the Title Suit No. 11 of 1995 and consequently allowed both the appeals. Being aggrieved, Mahtabuddin obtained the Rules. 

5. The High Court Division, after hearing both the Rules in Civil Revision No. 4612 of 2003 and Civil Revision No. 925 of 2004 together, found the Deed No. 6812 dated 12.10.1974, in favour of Mahtabuddin as genuine and also found possession in his favour. On these findings, the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division, made both Rules absolute. 

6. Mr. Bivash Chandra Biswas, the learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing on behalf of the petitioners, submits that the defendant in Title Suit No. 301 of 1976 and the plaintiff in Title Suit No. 11 of 1995 claimed ownership in the suit-land by virtue of a forged Deed of Sale but in spite of raising such a plea of forgery, he was not able to produce the original deed and filed only a certified copy, as such, the Appellate Court rightly disbelieved the said forged deed but the High Court Division .erred in law in disagreeing with the findings of fact arrived at by .the Appellate Court, the last Court of facts. 

7. We have heard the learned Advocate for the petitioners, perused the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division and also the judgments and decrees passed by the Courts below. 

8. It appears that Mahtabuddin Biswas, the predecessor of the respondents, claimed title in the suit-land, having an area of 1.66 acres of the lands in Plot Nos. 646, 601, 648 and 647 of Mouza Hizlakar, on the basis of a registered kabala Deed No. 6812 dated 12.10.1974, executed by one Indra Bhusan, the admitted original owner. But he was unable to produce the original deed and submitted only a certified copy of the same. This was not accepted by the Appellate Court as secondary evidence.

9. The High Court Division found that the defendant in Title Suit No. 301 of 1976, called for the concerned volume from the office of the District Registrar, Kushtia. Accordingly, one clerk from the said office brought the concerned volume in Court and after comparing the certified copy of the Deed No. 6812 with the concerned pages of the Volume, found the averments made in the certified copy to be identical with the statements made in the Volume. The said clerk deposed as DW.4 and proved that the concerned certified copy was issued by the .office of the concerned St& Registrar. The High Court Division found that this evidence adduced by the DW.4 was not denied on behalf of the plaintiffs in the Title Suit No. 301 of 1976. The High Court DiviSi6n also found that the plaintiff in the Title 'Suit No. 11 of 1995 proved his title as well as possession in the suit-land and made the Rules absolute.

10. The learned Advocate for the petitioners fails to dislodge any of the above findings of the High Court Division. 

11. Under such circumstances, these petitions merit no consideration and accordingly, those are dismissed. 

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 24th day of May, 2006 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2915 of 1997).
full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim C J: This Appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated the 24th day of May, 2006 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2915 of 1997 making the Rule absolute reversing the judgment and decree dated 07.05.1997 passed by the Additional District Judge, Sylhet in Title Appeal No.222 of 1994 reversing those dated 26.09.1994 passed by the Assistant Judge, Temporary Additional Court, Sadar, Sylhet in Title Suit No. 231 of 1992 dismissing the suit.

2. The facts involved in the case, in short, are that the suit land originally belonged to Dhan Bibi and Toyab Mia from whom Julfikar Ali and Majar Ali took jote settlement by executing a registered Kabuliyat dated 15 Sravan, 1283 B.S. concerning an area of 1 hal, 2 kedars and 2 jasti at a rental of TK. 4.50 per year and for arrear rents the landlord filed rent suit No. 132 of 1935 and got decree and while said Majar Ali was in possession transferred the suit land in favour of Masaddar Ali 35 years back and handed over title deeds and possession thereof and the said Masaddar Ali possessed the suit land by planting trees and bamboos and died 24 years back leaving behind the plaintiffs as his heirs who recent in the year 1982 came to know about the wrong record of rights in the names of defendants and on approach by them; Majar Ali, the proforma defendant No. 25 executed a registered deed of relinquishment on 21.04.1982 in their favour.

3. The defendant Nos. 1 (ka), 1 (kha), 2(ka)-(cha), 3, 12 and 15 contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter-alia, that Majar Ali after auction shifted to the other place and relinquished 6 kedars, 3 powas, 2 reks and 10 gondas of patit jungel in favour of Munir Miah, Chand Miah and others on executing a Sharanlipi dated 2nd Ashwin, 1362 B.S. and regarding his non-relinquishment though the same has been recorded in the name of Majar Ali, 1 the plaintiffs corrected the same in their favour by filing case before the Revenue Authority and accordingly, prayed for dismissal of the suit.

4. Leave was granted to consider the submissions of Mr. Mahmudul Islam, learned Counsel, for the appellant that the findings of the High Court Division are that the suit itself suffers from defect of patties for not substituting the heirs of the deceased proforma defendant who admitted the correctness of the plaintiff case in his written statement. The learned Counsel further submitted that the High Court Division has failed to appreciate. the evidentiary value of a Muktipotra if the said document is proved as a document regarding title and therefore, non-consideration I of so on a document while passing the judgment by the High Court Division results in erroneous decision and the lower appellate Court in its judgment fully considered the legal effect of 'Shoronlipi' and 'a rent receipt' as produced by the D.W.'s and came to a specific finding that such Shoronlipi and 'rent receipt' cannot be treated under the facts and circumstances of the present case document to be relied on or on the basis of which the title of the defendants as claimed could not be established but the High Court Division without applying it's judicial mind came to an erroneous finding. In addition, Mr. Islam submitted that in the absence of any legal infirmity in the findings of fact arrived at by the Court of Appeal, the High Court Division committed error in interfering with the decision of the Court of Appeal below. Mr. Islam also submitted that proforma defendant No. 25 having admitted the sale of the suit land in favour of the predecessor of the plaintiffs by a registered document and also admitting possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land for over twelve years, the High Court Division erred in law in interfering with the finding of facts of the Court of Appeal below that the plaintiffs filed the suit within the period of limitation after coming to know of the wrong recording of the suit land in the record of rights".

5. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, learned Counsel, appearing for the appellants submitted that the findings of the High Court Division are that the suit itself suffers from defect of parties for not substituting the heirs of the deceased pro-forma defendant who admitted the correctness of the plaint case in his written statement. The learned Counsel further submitted that the High Court Division has failed to appreciate the evidentiary value of a Muktipotra if the said document is proved as a document regarding title and therefore, non-consideration of such a document while passing the judgment by the High Court Division results in erroneous decision and the lower appellate Court in its judgment fully considered the legal effect of 'Shoronlipi and 'a rent receipt' as produced by the D.W.'s and came to a specific finding that such 'Shoronlipi' and 'rent receipt' cannot be treated under the facts and circumstances of the present case, a document to be relied on or on the basis of which the title of the defendants as claimed could not be established but the High Court Division' without applying it's judicial mind came to an erroneous finding. In addition, Mr. Islam submitted that in the absence of any legal infirmity in the findings of fact arrived at by the Court of Appeal, the High Court Division committed error in interfering with the decision of the Court of Appeal below. Mr. Islam also submitted that proforma defendant No.25 having admitted the sale of the suit land in favour of the predecessor of the plaintiffs by a registered document and also admitting  possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land for over twelve years, the High Court' Division erred in law in interfering with the finding of facts of the Court of Appeal below that the plaintiffs filed the suit within   the period of limitation after coming to know of the wrong recording of the suit land in the record of rights.

<u>6. Mr. M. A. Mannan, learned Counsel, appearing for the respondents submitted that the heirs of defendant No.25 who died after filing written statement, being necessary parties in the suit having not been substituted, the suit is apparently bad for defect of party; that the plaintiffs failed to prove the alleged story of transfer of the suit land by defendant No.25 to Masaddar Ali, plaintiffs' predecessor either by executing any document or by adducing any evidence as payment of any consideration money, delivery of possession, and more particularly when P.W.1 in his deposition stated that except his oral statement there is no other material to show when and how the transfer took place, and in that view of the matter the claim of their acquisition of title relinquishment but that does not confer any title to the plaintiffs and the statement made in the said document is not sufficient to hold that the plaintiffs could establish their title to the suit land as the same is not a document of transfer; that the writ statement filed by the defendant No.25 was not proved by any body as such, the statement allegedly therein do not deserve to be considered by any Court of law but the Court of Appeal below acted illegally in taking into consideration said written statement. The learned Counsel further submitted that the Court of Appeal below erroneously held that by the unregistered 'Shoronlipi no title passed to the defendants, having failed to notice that the defendant No.25 was holding the jote right (tenancy right) only while superior interests remained with the defendants landlord and as such, relinquishment by 'Shoronlipi' and by endorsement in the back of the counterfoil of rent receipt was sufficient to pass title to the defendants who were landlords of defendant No. 25; that the defendants adduced documentary evidence in support of their possession in the suit land and they proved the factum of possession by adducing evidence in respect of manner of possession inasmuch as they in their written statement stated that they possess the suit land by growing winter vegetables and also paddy in some portion of the same and the witnesses of possession D.W.'s 3 and 4 unequivocally supported the defendant's possession in the suit land but the Court of Appeal below on a misreading of the evidence on record arrived at an erroneous findings of possessing in favour of the plaintiffs. The learned Counsel finally submitted that it is the case of the defendants that out of /14/ annas share of kabuliyat land, the defendant No.25 relinquished 6 kedars 3 powas 2 reks 10 gondas of land in favour of the landlord by executing 'Shoranlipi' and also by endorsement on the counterfoil of the rent receipt and defendant No. 25 retained 5 kedars 2 powas 1 jaista out of the kabuliyat   land and RW. 1 in his deposition did not deny the said assertion and this fact coupled with 'Shoronlipi proved the case of the defendant.</u>

7. We have heard the learned Counsel of both sides. On perusal of the record it appears that it is the allegation of the plaintiffs that his father after his grandfather, Zulfiqur Ali became the owner and possessor of the suit land P.W.1, Md. Torun Mia deposed in support of his case. During cross-examination P.W.1 admitted that the rent suit against Zulfiqur Ali was filed. The predecessor of the plaintiffs lost his right in auction. It was further admitted that there was no registered deed of transfer   between the parties regarding the suit land. The plaintiffs claim by exhibit-1 is not satisfactorily proved. How the plaintiffs proved themselves to be the successor of the suit land, when the other heirs of Zulfiqur Ali has not been brought into record. Plaintiffs' father Masaddar Ali's purchase story could not be substantiated by producing documentary evidence. P.W.1 himself in cross-examination admitted that except his oral statement, there is no iota of evidence, to show what transfer took place. The plaintiffs further claimed that defendant No. 25 relinquished the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs by way of registered decd. P.W.2 Mukul Mia stated that the defendants are in possession of the suit land. He is also a solitary eye witness of exhibit-5. He seems to be unaware of the contents of the document. P.W.3, Abdur Noor, stated that he does not know in whose name the suit land has been recorded. P.W.4 also gave a contradictory statement regarding the mode of securing and acquiring title of the plaintiffs. It appears from the statement of P.W.'s that none could prove the title of the plaintiffs' predecessors over the suit land.

<u>8. It appears that the alleged sale deed has not been proved by sufficient evidence. It appears that the plaintiffs have not acquired any right, title and interest through memorandum. It is beyond doubt as per documentary and oral evidence that plaintiffs right of accruing or acquiring title remains discrepant and uncorroborated. It further appears that exhibit-5 does not confer any title upon the plaintiffs. The executant of exhibit-5 has not come before the Court to substantiate the plaintiffs claims. The plaintiffs have failed to prove the exclusive possession of their vendors.</u>

9. From the documents adduced by the defendants it appears that the defendants are in possession of the suit land. All the D.W.'s have categorically denied the plaintiffs possession over the suit land.

10. It appears that there is no finding regarding the document exhibited by the defendants particularly the 'Swaranlipi executed by the admitted tenant in favour of the admitted landlords and the alleged endorsement by the tenant on the counter-foil of the rent receipt issued by the admitted landlords regarding the relinquishment of their tenancy, these two vital documents were not at all considered though the defendants made specific assertion on the basis of such documents. In absence of any finding regarding these documents, it appears that the Court of Appeal below failed to decide whether the defendant End. No. 25, Syed Mazer Ali had got any right, title and interest in the suit land at the relevant time, in the absence of such right, title, he had no authority to issue any 'Muktipatra' in favour of anybody as alleged by the plaintiffs. Moreover, admittedly the defendant No. 25 had expired during pendency of the suit land and his successors ought to have been substituted in the suit, though no where in the record it is appeared that nobody claimed that the defendant No. 25 has no successor in the world. The Court of Appeal below also considered the written statement of the defendant No. 25 in arriving into his decision though its contention was not approved by anybody.

<u>11. The High Court Division observed that the suit suffers from defect of parties and no contention of the defendant No. 25 in his written statement which was not proved by anybody, was illegally considered   beyond the scope of law; that the plaintiffs were known about their alleged wrong recording since long time but they did not file any suit within six years from date of their knowledge and hence the suit is barred by limitation. The High Court Division further observed that the suit was decreed on the basis of a document which cannot be treated as a deed of acquiring title by anybody. It appears from Section 100 of Sylhet Tenancy Act that the said provision is not at all relevant to the instant suit.</u>

12. In view of the above, we find no substance in the submissions of the learned Counsel for the appellants.

13. Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.

End.

case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 27.01.2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2877 of 1999)
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J.:- This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 27.01.2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2877 of 1999 discharging the Rule and affirming the judgment and decree dated 30.06.1999 passed in Title Appeal No. 03 of 1996 by the then Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), First Court, Comilla, allowing the appeal setting aside the judgment and decree dated 30.10.1995 passed in Title Suit No. 52 of 1985 by the Assistant Judge, Barura, Comilla dismissing the suit on contest.

2. The facts, leading to the filing of this petition for leave to appeal, in a nutshell, are:

3. Abdur Rahman, the predecessor-in-interest of respondent Nos. 1-7 as the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 52 of 1985 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Barura, Comilla impleading the respondents and the predecessor in interest of the petitioners as defendants in the suit. Plaintiffs case is that while possessing the 2nd scheduled land, Syed Osman Haider Chowhdury sold the land in favour of defendant No. 1 by a registered deed of sale dated 13.04.1975. The plaintiff stated that he is the contiguous owner of the 2nd scheduled land and. after obtaining certified copy of the deed, the plaintiff came to know about the deed of sale dated 19.09.1976 and filed Pre-emption Case No. 208 of 1976. After that, the pre-emption case was renumbered as Pre-emption Case No. 40 of 1983. The plaintiff further stated that in that pre-emption case, the defendant stated that the deed of sale under pre-emption was a 'nadabi' deed and to that effect the defendant obtained compromise decree. After that, the plaintiff came to know about the fraudulent decree while searching Title Suit No. 287 of 1977. The plaintiff was not made a party to the alleged compromise decree and the defendants obtained the said fraudulent compromise decree to defeat right of pre-emption of the plaintiff. He further stated that the alleged compromise decree is illegal, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiff. Hence the suit has been filed.

4. Defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint. His case, in short, is that Charag Ali Munshi, father of the defendant got title and possession of the suit land after obtaining settlement. After that, he died leaving behind four sons and three daughters as heirs and by amicable settlement, defendant No. 1 and his brother, Tofazzal got possession of the suit land as well as other land. The defendant stated that during S.A. operation, the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of defendant No. 2 and for that reason defendant No. 2 executed and registered the alleged 'nadabi' deed in favour of defendant No. 1. The scribe mistakenly wrote the deed, of sale in place of 'nadabi' deed. As such, defendant No. 1 filed Title Suit No. 487 of 1977 before the then Third Munsif Court (now Assistant Judge), Comilla and defendant Nos. 1 and 2 obtained decree by way of solenama. The defendant 'further stated that the plaintiff knew about the compromise decree of Title Suit No. 487 of 1977 and the sole compromise decree was legally obtained by the defendant and that the plaintiff on false statements filed the suit.

5. The trial Court by its judgment and 14 order dated 30.10.1995 dismissed the suit.

6. Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No. 03 of 1996 before the District Judge, Comilla and on transfer, the appeal was heard and disposed of by the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Second Court, Comilla, who by his judgment and order dated 30.06.19.96 allowed the same setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court.

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the appellate Court, the defendants filed a revisional application before the High Court Division and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 2877 of 1999. After hearing the parties, the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division, by the judgment and order dated 27.01.2009 discharged the Rule.

8. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the leave-petitioners have filed this civil petition for leave to appeal before this Division.

9. Mr. Syed Amirul Islam, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the leave-petitioners, submits that respondent Nos. 2-4 did not have locus standi to file the instant suit and that the High Court Division erroneously concurred with the findings of the appellate Court and as such, the impugned judgment should be set aside. He further submits that respondent Nos. 2-4 had the knowledge of filing the suit as it is evident from written objection file by the leave-petitioners and that the suit filed by respondent Nos. 2-4 challenging the compromise decree passed in Title Suit No. 287 of 1977 was fraudulent and as such, the impugned judgment delivered by the High Court Division should be set aside.

10. Mr. Nikhilesh Datta, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of respondent Nos. 2-4, on the other hand, supports the impugned judgment.

11. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates, perused the impugned judgment and the materials on record.

12. The salient findings of the High Court Division, in brief, are as under:

<u>13. Plaintiff-respondent No. 1 as the pre-emptor filed Pre-emption Case No. 208 of 1976 renumbered as Pre-emption Case No. 40 of 1983 against the deed of sale dated 13.04.1975 registered during the pendency of the aforesaid pre-emption case. Purchaser-respondent No. 1 filed Title Suit No. 487 of 1977 on 12.11.1977 praying for declaration that the deed of sale dated 20.03.1975 was a 'nadabi' deed and obtained compromise decree on 20.12.1977 within a span of 38 days. The trial Court did not consider the case of the plaintiff-respondent in its proper perspective and erroneously found that plaintiff-respondent No. 1 had no locus standi to file the suit. The subsequent change of deed of sale into a 'nadabi' deed was done to frustrate the right of pre-emption. The judgment and decree obtained in Title Suit No. 488 of 1977 was fraudulent. Fraud vitiates everything.</u>

14. The aforesaid findings of the High Court Division having been based on proper appreciation of laws and facts do not call for interference.

<u>15. Mr. Syed Amirul Islam, learned Senior Advocate, contends that the suit was hopelessly barred by limitation and that the appellate Court and the High Court Division erroneously found that the suit was not barred by limitation. Such a contention is of no. avail as limitation would run from the date of actual knowledge of the decree delivered in Title Suit No. 487 of 1977 and that the suit was filed within the statutory period of limitation as soon as the plaintiff-respondent came to know of the impugned decree. What is important to note here is than the defendant-petitioner did not file the certified copy of the decree in the pre-emption case. A mere statement of obtaining a decree in the written objection of the pre-emption case is not sufficient for reckoning the period of limitation.</u>

16. In the light of the findings made before, we do not find any substance in this civil petition. Accordingly, this civil petition for leave to appeal is dismissed.

End.
