full_judgment:
S.K. Sinha J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 6th August, 2009 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division passed in Civil Revision No. 2070 of 2009.

<u>2. Short facts relevant for the disposal of this petition are that Sayed Abu Shayed, predecessor of the respondent Nos. 1-8, instituted Other Class Suit No.199 of 1976 against the petitioners and the respondent Nos. 9-15 for specific performance of contract. The said suit was decreed ex-parte. Thereafter the petitioners filed other class suit No. 27 of 2008 in the court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Mymensingh, for declaration of their title over the suit property, cancellation of Deed No.8964 dated 19th April, 1979 and further declaration that the decree passed in Other Class Suit No.199 of 1976 is void, illegal, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiffs. Their case is that the suit land belonged to Bisheshwar Dutta and his three brothers. Respondent Nos. 9-10 Ashok Kumar and Renuka Rani Dutta the successive heirs of Bisheswar did not enter into any contract for sale of suit, Plot No.783 with Syed Abu Shayed or with Dr. Helal Uddin, the predecessor of respondent Nos. 16-19. Sayed Abu Shayed created   a forged deed of contract and filed the suit and obtained a collusive ex-parte decree on 26th June, 1977 and in pursuance of the said decree, he got a sale deed executed through Court on 19th April, 1979.</u>

3. The respondent Nos. 1-8 have been contesting the suit by filing written statement, denying all materials allegations made in the plaint. Their case is that Ashoke Kumar Dutta and Renuka Rani Dutta as heirs of late Bisheswar Dutta entered into a contract for sale of some lands of suit plot with Sayed Abu Shayed for a consideration of Tk. 5,000/- and thereafter the respondent No. 9 Ashoke Kumar Dutta entered another deed of contract for sale of 8 decimals of land from suit Plot No. 783 with Syed Abu Shayed for a consideration of Tk. 1,000. Thereafter Sayed Abu Shayed requested the respondent Nos.9 and 10 for executing and registering the sale deed but they refused his request and consequent upon which, he instituted Other Class Suit No.199 of 1976 in the 2nd Court of Assistant Judge, Mymensingh against the plaintiff petitioners; Bhabesh Chandra Shaha and the respondent Nos.9 and 10 for specific performance of contract and obtained ex-parte decree on 28th June, 1976 and that in execution of the decree they obtained a deed through Court on 19th April, 1979 and that the predecessor of the respondent No.3 and the petitioners filed a Miscellaneous Case No. 111 of 1981 under Order 9, Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the said decree. The said case was dismissed for default on 30th April, 1982 against which they filed another Miscellaneous Case No.119 of 1982 under Order 9 Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure but the same was also dismissed and then the petitioners moved District Judge, Mymensingh in Civil Revision No. 106 of 1982 against the judgment and order passed in Miscellaneous Case No.119 of 1982 and the same also dismissed on contest on 29th July, 1987, against which judgment, they moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1033 of 1987. A Single Bench of the High Court Division discharged the rule, that against the judgment of the High Court Division, the petitioners moved the Appellate Division in Civil Petition No.1739 of 2008 which was dismissed on 8th April, 2009 and that the respondents deeds have been acted upon. The petitioners with a view to prevent the operation of Execution Case No. 27 of 1978 filed the present suit with false allegations and as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed.

4. The petitioners on 7th May, 2009 filed an application in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge for staying all further proceedings of Other Class Execution Case No.27 of 1978 till disposal of Other Class Suit No.27 of 2008 pending in the Court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Mymensingh. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Mymensingh by order dated 20th May, 2009 rejected the prayer for stay. The petitioners then unsuccessfully moved the District Judge, Mymensingh in a revision petition and then they moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2070 of 2009.

5. Mr. Abdus Salam Khan, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioners, argued that the Teamed Single Judge of the End. High Court Division erred in law in not staying the further proceedings of the execution case in failing to consider that law enjoins the Court to make an order of stay since a suit is pending between the parties in respect of the same subject matter and thus, unless the proceedings of the execution case are stayed, the very purpose for filing the suit will be frustrated. He further submits that the decision of the learned District Judge is not at all a speaking order and since it suffers from non-consideration of materials on record, the High Court Division without applying its judicial mind shirked its responsibility and as such, the judgment of the High Court Division merits interference by this Court.

<u>6. We have heard the learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners and perused the connected papers including the impugned judgment. Admittedly the petitioners instituted Miscellaneous Case No. 119 of 1976 for setting aside the ex-parte decree passed in Other Class Suit No. 119 of 1976. After the dismissal of the case, they again filed Miscellaneous Case No. 111 of 1981 which was also dismissed. Thereafter they moved the High Court Division and the Appellate Division, and 1 after exhausting all remedies available to them, they instituted the present suit after more than 10 years of passing the decree. On consideration of the above facts, we find no substance in the points raised. The High Court Division upon correct assessment of the materials on record arrived at a correct decision and discharged the rule. We therefore find no reason to interfere with the same.</u>

7. The petition is, therefore, dismissed.

End.

full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim J: These Petitions for Leave to Appeal are directed against the common judgment and order dated 24.02.2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision Nos. 3310 of 2002 and 3320 of 2002 discharging  in the Rules arising  out of the judgment and decree dated 31.03.2002 passed by the Additional District Judge 3rd Court, Sylhet in Title App No. 208 of 1999 heard analogously with Title Appeal No. 209 of 1999 allowing the appeals reversing those dated 23.11.1998 passed by the Assistant Judge, Sylhet Sadar, Sylhet in Title Suit No. 17 of 1996 heard analogously with Title Suit No. 103 of 1996 decreeing the suit.

<u>2. The facts of the cases, in short, are that Babu Shailendra Kumar Purkayestha and Nogendra Kumar Purkayestha were mirasdars and owners of the suit land and the plaintiff took jote settlement of the suit land from them before the commencement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the plaintiff paid rents year to year to the said Mirashdars and obtained cheque forges thereof and being in possession of the suit land, the plaintiff constructed houses thereon though her bharatias on the basis of the right of adverse possession acquiring title and possession thereof and during the last survey, the suit land was it, wrongly recorded in the name of the father of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and that their father by executing registered deed of muktipatra dated 16.10.1997 disowned his claim of wrong record relating to suit land within the knowledge of the defendant and the plaintiff after mutation of her name got separate khatian in her name. and was in possession of the suit land on payment of Government rents and constructed pucca walls and kutcha house and possessing the same through different tenants and the plaintiff also grew paddy on some portion of land and transferred 6 decimals of land to Abdul Masabbir, who after his purchase has been possessing the same by constructing pucca houses and boundaries and installed electric connection and paying bills thereof and the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in collusion with defendant No.3 managed to issue a notice against the plaintiff alleging to annul mutation in the name of the plaintiff and defendant Nos. 1 and 2 threatened the plaintiff of dispossession from the suit land and hence the suit.</u>

3. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations stating, inter alia, that the plaintiff's suit has no case of action, the suit is not maintainable and it is hit by limitation and Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and defendant Nos.1 and 2 as heirs of their father Rosmoy datta, were the owners in possession of the suit land; the brother in law of the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 103 of 1996 for declaration that the document is void and the plaintiff mutated her name in the record of the suit land illegally and secretly and when defendants submitted objection, the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 17 of 1996 and although Rosmoy Datta died in the year 1985, the plaintiff could not get anything with the help of the said muktipatra during his life time and the record in the suit land was prepared in the name of owner Rosmoy Datta, who took jote settlement of the suit land from its original owner by way of a patta; Shailendra Das and plaintiff's story of settlement was forged and the defendants are in possession of the rest land and defendants filed Title Suit No.103 of 1996 for recovery of possession of the suit land; the plaintiff created some papers in favour of Hasan Khatun and inducted her into possession on .0550 decimals of land within the suit land including a total land of .06 18 decimals which was under the possession of the plaintiff by force and for recovery of the same the said suit was filed and the plaintiff's suit has been filed with false statement which is liable to be dismissed.

4. Mvi. Md. Wahidullah, learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing for the petitioner submitted that the High Court Division committed error of law in passing the impugned judgment and order discharging the Rule without any independent finding on merit of the suit but merely relied upon the findings of the Court of appeal passing the judgment of reversal without adverting to the material findings and reasoning of the trial Court as to possession of the plaintiff-petitioners in the suit land with reference to the evidence on record; that upon taking needless efforts in search of title of the plaintiff-petitioner in connection with Title Suit No.17 of 1996 which is merely a suit for permanent injunction wherein the determination of dispute of possession of the contending parties in the suit land is the paramount consideration and the Court should not go into deep for deciding title of parties; that the plaintiff petitioner by collateral evidence of title at least on the date of proposition of the khatian, rent receipts in her name supported by consistent oral evidence of as many as 8 P.Ws; proved her act of possession in the suit land as against the alleged claim of the defendant respondents having no documents in their names, failed to prove their possession in the suit land. The learned Advocate further submitted that both the High Court Division and the Court of Appeal below committed error of law and arrived at wrong finding upon misconstruction and misreading of the local inspection report and the sketch map, exhibit- 10 and 10(a) which are not in contradiction with the plaintiff-petitioners claim as wrongly held by the High Court Division and the Court of Appeal; rather the said report and the map depict the actual nature and position of the suit land supporting the claim of the plaintiff Petitioner.

<u>5. It appears from the record that the plaintiff filed Title Suit No.17 of 1996 for permanent injunction which was decreed in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner but on appeal the decision of the trial Court was reversed by the Court of Appeal below. The respondent instituted Title Suit No.103 of 1996 for declaration that the registered nadabinama dated 16.10.79 executed and registered by Rosmoy Dutta, predecessor, in favour of defendant No.1, regarding the suit land is illegal, forged and not binding on the respondent and also for recovery of khas possession of the suit land. It appears that an Advocate commissioner held a local inspection and submitted report before the Court being exhibited 10 and 10A wherein it was stated that the land in dispute is not the same land in dispute, although the plaintiff in Title Suit No.178 of 1996 i.e. the present  petitioner clearly stated that she has homestead in the land in dispute, which is in contradictory to the report submitted by the Advocate Commissioner. It is the specific finding of the Court of appeal below that the petitioner could not prove by submitting documentary evidence that she has possession on the suit land for which the Court of appeal below found that the petitioner is not entitled to get a decree for permanent injunction. On the other hand, the Court of appeal below also found that the land which was the subject matter of the muktipatra and claimed by petitioner as the land in dispute is not the same land because the plaintiff of Title Suit No.17 of 1996 i.e. the present petitioner failed to prove that they obtained settlement from the Zamindar by submitting dakhilas for which the said nadabipatra is not binding upon the them. The Court of appeal below found that from the perusal of the cheque/dakhilas, exhibit-2 series and the certified copy of the patta, exhibit-'Kha', that although in the cheque/dakhilas the name of the pattadar was found but the identification of the suit land and the patta number were not mentioned in it correctly. The certified copy of the patta, exhibit kha, as produced by the opposite party, shows that the land is number patta within the land of old 201/1 to 209/2 it could not be ascertained as to whether the dakhilas exhibited before the Court were related to the disputed land or not. The Court of appeal below also found that the same person   put the signatures of Shailendra Kumar and Nagendra Kumar in the dakhilas and the petitioner did not take any step to get the signatures proved for which the Court of appeal below found that the cheque/dakhilas of the settlement which were exhibited by way of exhibit 2 series are forged and concocted and were prepared in order to prove title in the name of the Zaminder inasmuch as in the cheque dakhilas there is no reference of patta number.</u>

6. In view of the above, we find no substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner.

7. Accordingly, the petitions are dismissed.

End.

full_judgment:
Md. Tafazzul Islam J: This petition for leave to appeal arises out of the judgment and order dated 18th April, 2004 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2584 of 1994 discharging the Rule which was obtained against the judgment and decree dated 30.04.94 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Jhenidah in Title Appeal No. 186 of 1990 affirming those of dated 24.06.90 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Jhenidah in Title Suit No. 412 of 1987 dismissing the suit.

<u>2. The petitioners instituted above Title Suit No. 412 of 1987 seeking declaration of title and confirmation of possession in the suit land stating, inter alia, that Thomas Twudi possessed the suit land through bargadars and Rakhal Chandra Ghosh and others were the holders of rent  receiving interests; Thomas Twudi settled the suit land to Nagendra Bala who while in possession, on 25th Falgoon, 1358 B.S. settled the suit land to Sonaullah, father of the petitioners and then Sonaullah in Agrahayan. 1362 B.S, executed and registered a kabuliat in favour of Nagendra Bala; after the death of Sonaullah the petitioners inherited the property left by Sonaullah; the defendant No.1, on 15th Kartic 1394 B.S, on the basis of the record of right prepared in his name, denied the title of the petitioners in the suit land and threatened to dispossess them therefrom and hence the suit.</u>

3. That defendant Nos. 8 to 9 contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter alia, that Thomas Twudi cultivated neel in the suit land and when neel cultivation was stopped he went back to England and then Rakhal Chandra Ghosh and others, the landlords, took back the khas possession of the suit land; Rakal Chandra Ghosh died leaving behind son Satish Chandra and wife Shaila Bala; Ratikanta, another co-sharer landlord, also died leaving behind four sons namely, Mohadeb, Anil, Azit and Raj Krishna; Jagabandhu, another co-sharer landlord, also transferred his 1/3 share to Rani Bibi by an exchange; Anil, Azit and Raj Krishna by three registered deeds dated 24.06.69, 23.02.70 and 07.08.72 transferred their lands in favour of Azazuddin, Nurul Islam and Daliluddin; there is a tank within suit plot No. 713 and non-suit plot No. 712 and the major portion of suit plot No. 713 is the bank of the tank; a hat has been established on Plot Nos. 703, 704, 714, 715, 718 and 722; Rani Bibi by deed dated 20.01.1979 gifted her share of land to Md. Ismail Mondal who by deed dated 11.04.1987 gifted the same to Daliluddin Primary School; the plaintiffs who are landless persons have been residing in a portion of the suit land by permission of the former Chairman of the local Union Council and Sahidul Islam and Bazlur Rahman have also been possessing a portion of the suit land by taking lease from the Chairman of the local Union Council. The trial court after hearing dismissed the suit. The petitioners then filed appeal and the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Jhenidah, after hearing, dismissed the appeal. The petitioner then moved the High Court Division and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 2584 of 1994 and after hearing the High Court Division discharged the Rule.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the High Court Division failed to consider that the father of the petitioners had been possessing the suit land since Falgun, 1658 B.S. and after his death the petitioners are possessing the suit land; because of their long possession for over 37 years since 1358 B.S. the petitioners acquired possessory title in the suit land; in view of the provisions of section 110 of the Evidence Act the possession of the petitioners are referable to the settlement made in favour of their predecessor Sonaullah in the year 1358 B.S.; the oral evidence of D.Ws. denying their purchase of .05 decimals of the land from the petitioners by registered Kabala is not at all admissible in view of the provisions of section 91 and 92 of the Evidence Act; in view of the provisions of Order 7 Rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure the appellate Court ought to have decreed the suit in respect of 85 decimals out of 90 decimals of land excluding .05 decimals of land which was purchased by Fazlur Rahman and Abdus sobhan form the petitioners; the High Court Division failed to consider that the trial courts as well as the appellate Court misread and misconstrued the evidence on record which clearly established the possession of the petitioners in the suit land for over 37 years and also acquiring of title by settlement made in favour of Sonaullah in the year 1358 B.S.

5. As it appears the trial court dismissed the suit on the findings that Kabuliyet Ext. 1 (C) dated 14.12.1955 had no legal validity after 13.12.1955 in view of the provisions of section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950; the petitioners claimed that they acquired title to the suit land on the basis of their settlement by Nagendra Bala to Sonaullah, the predecessor of the petitioners but could not prove that they possessed the entire suit land; the suit is also bad for non joinder of Abdus Sobhan and Bazlur Rahman in the suit. The lower appellate court dismissed the appeal on the findings that the documents of settlement on the basis of which the petitioners claimed title, being forged, the petitioners did not acquire any title to the suit land; the petitioners not being in possession of the entire suit land are not entitled to a decree for declaration of title to the suit land; the petitioners by amendment of the plaint claimed relief for confirmation of possession along with declaration of title but did not put in requisite court fees for the relief of confirmation of possession.

<u>6. As it appears the High Court Division discharged the Rule holding that both the courts below concurrently found that the plaintiffs could not prove their possession in the entire suit land; the decisions cited by the learned Advocate of the petitioners do not support the contention of the petitioners that a decree may be passed even if the plaintiff is found not in possession of the entire suit land and the settled law is that in a suit for declaration of title and confirmation of possession if the plaintiff fails to prove his possession in the entire suit land he is not entitled to a decree even if he proved his title to the suit land; though Exts.4 and 4(A), the rent receipts, are not forged as found by the appellate court but even then this position will not in any way improve the case of the petitioners as they failed to prove their possession in the entire suit land.</u>

7. We are of the view that the High Court Division on proper consideration of the materials on record and applying the principle of law as applicable arrived at a correct decision and there is not cogent reason to interfere with the same.

8. The petition is dismissed.

End.

full_judgment:
Md. Muzammel Hossain J. This petition for leave to appeal under Article 103 of the Constitution of Peoples' Republic of Bangladesh is directed against the judgment and order dated 26.10.2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4361 of 1999 discharging the Rule upon affirming the judgment and decree dated 20.07.1999 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No.92 of 1997 dismissing the appeal thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 09.04.1997 passed by the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.186 of 1996 dismissing the suit.

2. The petitioner and his brother as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.310 of 1984 in the Court of Sub-Ordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka for declaration of title by way of adverse possession of the suit land and that the registered deeds of sale dated 15.11.1971, 05.12.1983 and 14.12.1983 are false, fabricated and not binding upon the plaintiffs. Thereafter the suit was transferred to the 5th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and re-numbered as Title Suit No.186 of 1996.

3. The plaintiffs' case, in short, is that the suit property originally belonged to C.S. recorded tenants Sree Luxmi Narayan and Rajendra Lal Sharma. Rajendra Lal Sharma died leaving behind only son Bholanath Sharma. The predecessor of the plaintiffs entered into the suit land at about 100 years ago and while living therein peacefully having uninterrupted possession he died on 16.7.1953 leaving behind the plaintiffs and their brother Ranjit Kumar Roy as legal heirs. Ranjit Kumar Roy, brother of the plaintiffs left the country before partition of the country. While the plaintiffs were living in the suit land they came to learn that one Zobeda Khatun purchased the suit land from Bholanath Sharma and she filed Title Suit No. 237 of 1960 for ejectment before the 6th court of Munsif Dhaka and the plaintiffs contested the suit by filing written statement and the said suit was dismissed. Zobeda Khatun did not claim the rent of the suit land thereafter and the plaintiffs did not admit her as the landlord. The so-called deed of sale in favour of Zobeda Khatun is false. Zobeda Khatun recorded her name in S.A. Khatian and mutated her name in the City Corporation but she never paid any tax.

4. The defendant no. 1 filed an application to the city Corporation for mutation of his name and notices were duly served upon the plaintiffs who filed written objection against the said application. The defendant no. 1 filed registered deed of sale dated 15.11.1971 to the City Corporation and the plaintiffs for the first time came to learn that Zobeda Khatun had sold the suit property to the defendant no.1 and thereafter the plaintiffs came to that the defendant no.1 sold the same to the defendant no.2 and 3 by registered deeds of sale dated 5.12.1983 and 14.12.1983 respectively. The defendant Nos.2 and 3 claimed the suit land by way of purchase from the defendant no. 1. The defendant no. 1 never claimed the suit land and rent from the plaintiffs and never served any notice nor tried to dispossess the plaintiffs. The defendant no.1 purchased the suit land 12 years ago but he never asserted his right, title or possession openly and publicly. The deed of sale of the defendant no.1 is false, fabricated and the defendant no.2 and 3 purchased the same from the defendant no.1 so the defendant nos.2 and 3 never acquired any right and title by way of the so-called deeds of sale. The plaintiffs have been in possession of the suit land for a long period of time and thus they have acquired title in the suit land by way of adverse possession and the deeds of sale of the defendant nos.2 and 3 are false and fabricated documents which are not binding upon the plaintiffs. Hence the suit for declaration of title by adverse possession and for declaration that the deeds are false, fabricated and not binding upon the plaintiffs.

5. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter-alia, that the suit land admittedly belonged to Rajendra Lal Sharma who constructed a building thereon in the year 1953 and enjoyed by letting out the same to tenants. Rajendra Lal Sharma died leaving behind his only heir Bholanath Sharma who mutated his name in the city Corporation and paid all taxes and the plaintiffs were the tenants under him. Thereafter Zobeda Khatun purchased the disputed land from Bholanath Sharma in 1954 by way of deed of sale and it was mentioned in the said deed that the plaintiffs were the tenants and they have right to recover the rent from the plaintiffs. Bholanath sold the disputed land after serving notices upon the plaintiffs to pay rent to Zobeda Khatun. Zobeda Khatun recorded her name in SA. Khatian and mutated her name with the city corporation and paid all taxes, Zobeda Khatun claimed rent from the plaintiffs several times but the plaintiffs did not pay the rent. Thereafter Zobeda Khatun filed a suit for ejectment against the plaintiffs and in the meantime the plaintiffs mutually agreed to vacate the suit land and accordingly Zobeda Khatun did not take any step and the said suit was dismissed for default. Zobeda Khatun sold the disputed land to the defendant no.1 and delivered physical possession to him. The defendant no. 1 having recorded his name in R.S. Khatian and mutated his name in the city corporation paid all taxes and thereafter sold the same to the defendant nos. 2 and 3 by two separate registered deeds of sale and delivered possession to them. The defendant nos. 2 and 3 claimed rent from the plaintiffs but the plaintiffs did not pay any rent and vacate the possession. The defendant nos. 2 and 3 served notices under section 106 of the T.P. Act upon the plaintiffs who replied to the said notices and thereafter the defendant nos. 2 and 3 filed a suit for ejectment before the Court of Assistant Judge and the same is pending for hearing.

6. The learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka by the judgment and decree dated 09.04.1997 dismissed Title Suit No.186 of 1996. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree the plaintiffs petitioners preferred appeal being Title Appeal No. 92 of 1997 in the Court or District Judge, Dhaka. The learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka by the judgment and decree dated 20.07.1999 dismissed the appeal. Thereafter being aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 20.07.1999 the plaintiffs-petitioners preferred revisional application before the High Court Division being Civil Revision No.4361 of 1999. A Single Bench of the High Court Division by the judgment and order dated 26.10.2008 discharged the Rule.

7. The plaintiffs-petitioners being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division preferred the instant civil petition for leave to appeal before this Court.

<u>8. We have heard Mr. Abdul Quayum, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, Mr. Mahmudul Islam, the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 2 and Mrs. Sofia Khatun, the learned Advocate-On-Record appearing for the respondent No. 4, perused the leave petition, impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division and all other connected papers on record. It appears that one Zobeda Khatun purchased the disputed land from Bholanath Sharma in 1954 by a registered deed of sale wherein it was mentioned that the plaintiffs were tenants and Zobeda Khatun has right to recover rent from them Bholanath served notices upon the plaintiffs to pay rent to Zobeda Khatun who recorded her name in S.A. Khatian and mutated her name in the City Corporation and paid all taxes. Thereafter Zobeda Khatun claimed rent from the Plaintiffs several times but they did not pay rent. Thereafter the ejectment suit was filed against the plaintiffs but they agreed to vacate the suit land and consequently Zobeda Khatun sold the suit land to the defendant No.1 and delivered physical possession to him. The defendant No.1 recorded his name in H.S. Khatian and mutated his name in the City Corporation and thereafter he sold the same to defendant Nos. 2 and 3 by separate registered deeds of sale and delivered possession. The plaintiffs failed to pay rent and vacate the suit land. The defendants filed suit against the plaintiffs for ejectment which is pending for disposal. The High Court Division have held that both the courts below made concurrent findings of facts that the plaintiffs are tenants in the suit land and that the plaintiffs claim of title by way of adverse possession is hit by Section 116 of the Evidence Act and thus the plaintiffs failed to prove their title in the suit land; that Zobeda Khatun and the Government were necessary parties in the suit but they were not impleaded in the suit. The High Court Division have rightly found that both the courts below on proper appreciation of the evidence on record made concurrent findings of facts which should not be interfered with as there was no misreading or non-consideration of the material evidence on record.</u>

9. In view of the above observations and findings we do not find any illegality in the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. In the premises we do not find any merit in the leave petition.

10. Accordingly, the leave petition is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 787 of 2010
lawyer:
Quamrul Haque Siddique, Advocate, instructed by Bivash Chandra Biswas, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner
A.J. Mohammad Ali, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md. Taufique Hossain, Advocate-on-record ------ For respondent Nos.1
For Respondent Nos. 2-3 None represented.
parties:
Md. Zahirul Islam ------ Petitioner.
Vs.
Md Mosharaf Hossain and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 22nd day of November, 2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 883 of 2006).
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah, J. This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated the 22nd day of November, 2009 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 883 of 2006 making the Rule absolute. Facts necessary for disposal of this petition are that petitioner as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 44 of 1996 in the Court of Assistant Judge, 5th Court, Gazipur for declaration that the Kabala being No. 2577 dated 07.02.1970 in favour of defendant No. 1 was illegal, collusive, fraudulent, forged, without any consideration and not binding and for recovery of khas possession as well.

2. The plaintiffs case, in short, was that the suit land originally belonged to Sattya Prashannya Ghose who having decided to settle in India madean exchange of his property with that of Sheikh Hashan Ali in India. But that time, EPDP Ordinance (in the plaint, the law was quoted like this was in force, so no deed of exchange could be made in favour of Sheikh Hashan Ali for which Sattaya Prashannya Ghose executed a power of attorney in his favour on 27.03.1964 in respect of 61 acres land including the suit land and handed over possession of the suit land to him. Hashan Ali submitted all the necessary papers to the Government of Bangladesh for registration of the said 61 acres land on the basis of power of attorney. In the meantime, Sheikh Hashan Ali died leaving behind two sons named Sheikh Zakir Hosain and Sheikh Iqbal Hossain and a widow. Then, on the prayer of said two sons of deceased Sheikh Hashan Ali, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Dhaka and the Officer-in-charge, Thana Public Health service Project section, Dhaka Division on 24.04.1996 by a registered deed being No. 12508 made permanent settlement of 21 acres land including the suit land in their favour. The said two sons of Hashan Ali transferred the suit land to the plaintiff by a registered kabala dated 05.01.1995 and delivered possession thereof to him and since then he has been in possession in the suit land. The suit land was neither vested nor abandoned. Sattya Prashannya Ghose did not transfer the suit land to defendant No. 1 by Kabala dated 07.02.1970, but he dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land forcibly on 12.02.1995.

3. In the plaint, it was specifically stated that the deed dated 07.02.1970 created cloud over plaintiffs title to the suit land and if that deed remained, there might be onslaught on his title to the suit land on the basis of the said deed, so the plaintiff was compelled to file the suit to remove the cloud over his title in the suit land.

4. The suit was contested by defendant Nos. 1 and 3 by filing two separate set of written statement (defendant No. 2 was the Sub-Registrar, Sreepur, Gazipur.

5. In the written statement filed by defendant No. 1. It was contended, inter alia, that Sattya Prashannya Ghose while had been in possession of the suit plot, he out of his necessity for money transferred 084 acre land in his favour by a kabala dated 07.02.1970 being deed No. 1577 and he delivered possession of the said transferred land to him. Sattya Prashannya Ghose transferred 1.98 acres land in favour of Aeat Ali by a registered Kabala dated 09.09.1994. Aeat Ali sold 10(ten) decimals land to the plaintiff and he is in possession thereof. Aeat Ali also sold some land to Aswani Kumar by a registered Kabala dated 10.12.1987 vide No. 13249. The plaintiff after purchasing the suit land from the title less person by the Kabala dated 15.01.2005 being No. 7795 filed Criminal Case No. 10 of 1995 which was rejected and possession of the defendant was proved. Sattya Prashannya Ghose, the actual owner of the suit land, never exchanged the suit land as claimed by the plaintiff.

6. In the written statement filed by defendant No. 3 (the Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner Gazipur), it was contended, inter alia, that Sattya Prashannya Ghose, the original owner of the suit land, having left for India, the suit property became an enemy property and was enlisted as vested property. The suit property is under the possession and control of the Government.

7. The suit was decreed by the trial Court by its judgment and decree dated 13.11.1997. Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court, defendant No. 1 preferred Title Appeal No. 207 of 1997 before the District Judge, Gazipur. The learned joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Gazipur having heard the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 05.10.2005 dismissed the appeal affirming those of the trial Court.

8. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court, defendant No. 1, filed Civil Revision No. 883 of 2006 before the High Court Division. A learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division after hearing the civil revision by the impugned judgment and order made the Rule absolute; hence this petition for leave to appeal. It may be stated that before the High Court Division, no one appeared on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite party.

9. Heard Mr. Qumrul Haque Siddique, learned Advocate, for the petitioner and Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, learned Counsel, who entered caveat on behalf of defendant No. 1.

<u>10. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute on the finding that "the plaintiff totally failed to prove his case and both the Courts below totally misunderstood and misconstrued the real fact and circumstance of the case. If a finding is not based on evidence on reasonable conclusion can be reached, then interference therewith in the Revision is justified plaintiff in order to succeed must establish his own case to obtain a decree and weakness of defendant's case is no ground for a decree in favour of the plaintiff."</u>

11. We have considered the plaint, the judgments and decrees of the Courts below and the deposition of the witness.

12. From the judgment and decree of the trial Court. It appears that it did not at all come to any finding as to when the plaintiff had been put into the possession of the suit land and on which date he was dispossessed, one of the relief's prayed for in the suit being for recovery of khas possession such finding was a must. The trial Court in a negative way found possession of the plaintiffs vendor and the plaintiff without coming to any finding in that respect with reference to the evidence on record. We consider it better to quote the finding of the trial Court which is as under:

“উপরোক্ত আলোচনা হইতে প্রমানিত যে, ইউ,পি,ডি,পি আইন প্রতিষ্ঠিত থাকায় শেখ হাসান আলী আর,এস, রেকর্ডেও সময় দলিল মূলে নালিশীমী দাবী করিতে না পারিলেও দখলে ছিলেন এবং আইনগত সমস্যার কারনে আর,এস, রেকর্ডটি তাহার নামে করিয়া নিতে পারেন নাই। যাহা হউক ইহা প্রমানিত যে, নালীশি জমিতে বাদী দাতার বৈধ অধিকার থাকাবস্থায় তাহার হস্তান্তর করায় নালিশী জমিতে বাদী স্বত্ব এবং ১নং বিবাদীর বৈধ স্বত্ব না থাকায় তাহার দখলটি অবৈধ (sic) এবং তাই বাদী নালীশি জমিতে খাস দখল পাইতে অধিকারী এবং ১ নং বিবাদীর নালিশী দলিলটি জাল বিধায় বাতিল করা হইল।”

13. In the context, it is necessary to state that in giving finding that Hashan Ali was in possession of the suit land at the time of R.S. record, no oral evidence was considered. The Appellate Court as the last Court of fact did not also consider the evidence in respect of possession of suit land and did not come to any finding whether the plaintiff had at all been put into the possession of the suit land after his purchase by the kabala dated 05.01.1995 and on which date he was dispossessed there from. It also found possession of the plaintiff in the suit land in a negative way as it observed “বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত তর্কিত রায়ে বাদীকে নালিশী সম্পত্তি হইতে বেদখলের বিষয় বিশদ আলোচনা না থাকিলে বাদীপক্ষ আরজী বর্ণিত কজ অব এ্যাকশন প্রমান করিলে (sic) সক্ষম হওয়ায় ইহা ধরিয়া নেওয়া যায় যে, বাদী নালিশী সম্পত্তি হইতে বেদখল হইবার তারিখে হইতে নির্দিষ্ট তামাদি মেয়াদের মধ্যে মূল মোকদ্দমাটি আনয়ন করিয়াছে।”

<u>14. Another important legal aspect of the case is that in the plaint the plaintiff himself admitted that because of the kabala being No. 2577 dated 07.02.1970, his title in the suit land was clouded; it was incumbent upon him to pray for declaration of title in the suit but he did not; so the suit for recovery of khas possession without the prayer for declaration of title was not maintainable.</u>

<u>15. From the judgment of the trial Court, it further appears that it considered the case of the defendant first and then cancelled the deed in question as forged. Such a procedure was totally wrong. When the plaintiff wanted to declare that the kabala in question was illegal, without consideration, fraudulent, void and not binding; onus was upon him to prove the deed to be so, and the trial Court was to consider the evidence of the plaintiff first in that respect, but it did not, and thus made a fundamental mistake in taking decision about the kabala in question. The Appellate Court simply endorsed the said finding of the trial Court without discussing the evidence on record. So, the theory of concurrent findings of fact cannot be applied in the case.</u>

16. In view of the above, we find no reason to interfere with the impugned judgment and order. Accordingly, the petition is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 266 of 2012
lawyer:
Quamrul Haque Siddique, Advocate instructed by Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on- Record ----- For the Petitioner 
Mr. Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, Senior Advocate instructed by Firozur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ----- For Respondent No. 1

parties:

Vs.
Majumder A. Salam and another ----- Respondents
case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 15.11.2011 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 355 of 2011)
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J.:- This Civil Petition for leave to Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 15. 11.2011 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 355 of 2011 discharging the rule.

<u>2. The necessary facts for disposal of this civil petition for leave to appeal, in short, are that the present leave-petitioner, as plaintiff, instituted Title Suit No. 51 of 2003 in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Court No. 1, Khulna against the present respondent No. 1 impleading him as defendant No. 1 and another for specific performance of contract. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that the defendant No. 1, being owner of the land described in schedule to the plaint, contracted to sell the same to the plaintiff at a consideration of Tk. 1,40,000/- and on receipt of earnest money of Tk. 80,000/- out of that contracted consideration money executed a bainapatra in fovour of the plaintiff on 05.05.1998 on condition that the defendant No. 1 would execute and register the sale deed on taking balance consideration money from the plaintiff. That subsequently also the defendant No. 1 took Tk. 50,000/- from the plaintiff on 02.11.2002 by giving a money receipt and also delivered possession of the land in favour of the plaintiff on 02.11.2002. But ultimately on 07.03.2003 the defendant No. 1 denied to execute and register the sale deed when the plaintiff requested him for the same and hence the suit.</u>

3. The defendant No. 1 appeared in that suit and filed written statement denying the genuineness of the impugned bainapatra. His specific case, as stated in the written statement, is that he never contracted to sell the suit land to the plaintiff, never executed any bainapatra in favour of the plaintiff and never took any money from the plaintiff. That some disputes arose in between the plaintiff and the defendant No. 1 relating to accounts in between 'them as they had business transactions and the plaintiff forcibly took some signatures of the defendant No. 1 on blank stamp papers on 30.08.1997 for which the defendant lodged a G.D. in the local police station; that the plaintiff might have created the impugned bainapatra using those signatures of the defendant No. 1 on the blank stamp papers; that the alleged bainapatra is forged, fraudulent and without consideration and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed.

4. During pendency of that suit the defendant No. 1 filed an application on 15.02.2010 for obtaining expert opinion a to the signature appearing in the disputed bainapatra and the money receipt and the learned Judge of the trial court, by the order dated 15.02.2010, allowed that application.

5. Being aggrieved by that order the plaintiff filed Civil Revision No. 31 of 2010 before the District Judge, 2nd Court Khulna which was ultimately heard and disposed of by the Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Khulna. By the judgment and order dated 13.10.2010 the Additional District Judge, Khulna rejected that revision affirming the order of the trail court allowing prayer for obtaining hand writing expert's opinion. The plaintiff then filed the above mentioned Civil Revision No. 355 of 2011 before the High Court Division and obtained rule. Ultimately a Single Bench of the High Court Division, by the impugned judgment and order dated 15.11.2011, discharged that rule upholding the judgment and order of the courts below.

6. Mr. Quamrul Haque Siddique, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-petitioner has made submissions before us to the effect that in this case the defendant has clearly admitted the signature appearing in the impugned bainapatra to be his own pleading a case to the effect that the plaintiff took this signature on the blank stamp papers forcibly and thereafter created the impugned bainapatra in that blank stamp papers containing the signature of the defendant- No. 1. The learned Advocate has contended that in spite of this clear defence case of the defendant No. 1 all the courts below allowed the prayer for examination of the signature of the defendant No. 1 appearing in the impugned bainapatra by a hand-writing expert unnecessarily and most whimsically and arbitrarily with-out applying judicial mind at all. The learned Advocate, however, has submitted that the signature of the defendant No. 1 in the money receipt, since not admitted by the defendant No. 1, can be examined by hand writing expert.

7. Mr. Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the defendant - respondent has made submissions to the effect that nowhere in the written statement the defendant No. 1 has admitted the signature appearing in the impugned bainapatra to be his own. The learned Counsel has contended that the plaintiff took some signatures of the defendant No. 1 forcibly and the defendant No. 1 has only expressed an apprehension that the plaintiff might have used those signatures of the defendant No. 1 in creating the impugned bainapatra. The learned Counsel has argued that in view of the written Statement of the defendant No. 1 it cannot be said that the defendant No. 1, admitted the signature appearing in the impugned bainapatra to he his own and in the circumstances examination of this signature by hand writing expert is necessary.

8. We have considered the submission of the learned Advocates of both the sides and gone through the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division, those of the courts below and also the written statement filed by the defendant-respondent.

9. From the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division it appears that this defendant-petitioner, in Miscellaneous Case No. 47 of 2004 deposed clearly as under:

“ও/পি, বাদী জোর করিয়া ৩০-১০-১৯৯৭ইং তারিখে একটি ষ্ট্যাম্প এ আমার স্বাক্ষর আদায় করেছিলেন। সেটাই বায়নায় রুপান্তর করেছে। বায়না পত্রের স্বাক্ষর জোর জবরদস্তি মূলক। রসিদের সই আমার নয়।”

10. It should be mentioned here that this suit was once decreed ex-parte and for setting aside that ex-parte decree the defendant No. 1 filed that Miscellaneous Case No. 47 of 2004. However, in view of the above quoted statements of the defendant No. 1 which he made in that Miscellaneous Case No. 47 of 2004 there remains no roam for argument that the defendant No. 1 did not admit the signature appearing in the impugned bainapatra as his own.

<u>11. So, in the circumstances, there is no necessity of examination of this signature of the defendant No. 1 appearing in the impugned bainapatra by hand writing expert. However, the signature appearing in the Money receipt, since not admitted by the defendant No. 1, may be examined by a hand writing expert.</u>

<u>12. The order for examination of the signature of the defendant No. 1 appearing in the impugned bainapatra by a hand writing expert, therefore, stands revoked.</u>

13. This Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal is thus disposed of summarily.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1336 of 2008
lawyer:
Zahirul Islam, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent No.1 
Respondent Nos.2-5 ------ Not represented

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 14.03.2007 passed the High Court Division in Civil Revision 1074 of 2004 with Civil Revision No. 928 of 2005 and Civil Rule No.928 of 2006)
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Aziz J. This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 14.03.2007 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.1074 of 2004 (heard analogous with Civil Rule No.928(R) of 2005 and Civil Rule No.17(R) of 2006) discharging the Rules thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 31.03.2004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Chandpur, in Title appeal No.41 of 2000 allowing the appeal and reversing those dated 02.03.2000 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 1st Court, Chandpur in Title Suit No.36 of 1994 dismissing the suit on contest.

2. The facts as set out in the memo of Civil Revision No.1074 of 2004, in short, are that the opposite-party No.1 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.36 of 1994 in the Court of the then Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Chandpur for declaration of title in the suit land stating, inter-alia, that the suit land comprising an area of .05 acres in plot No.931 under Khatian No 242 (formerly), corresponding to S. A. Khatian No.299 and .06 acres in both former and present plot No.931/969 of Monza 18 Dasdi under both District and Police Station-Chandpur are being owned and possessed by Durga Kumar Chakraborti and others from their predecessor, namely, Shamkanti Das alias Shamcharan Chakraborti. The predecessor of the plaintiff namely Gazi Nur Mohammad (now dead) as plaintiff brought Title Suit No. 3245 of 1958 in the Court of Munsif, 1st Court, Chandpur (relating to non suit land) for specific performance of contract, whereupon, a decree was passed on 04.04.1961 in favour of said plaintiff with Tk. 471.50 as cost. Thereafter, said Nur Mohammad obtained registered deed on 11.05.1963 through Court and then filed an Execution Case bearing No. 72 of 1963 for realization of alleged cost money. Plaintiff also purchased in auction as highest bidder, the land in suit along with other land and also took Bainama on 26.01.1992. Khatian No. 931 was mentioned wrongly in that Execution Case in place of correct C. S. Khatian No. 242 or S. A. Khatian No. 229 and plot No. 9301/969 but the boundary mentioned in auction was intact and that the land and its possession were handed over to plaintiff on 30.04.1992 after performing all formalities of auction sale and thus the case or execution of decree bearing No. 72 of 963 was disposed of on 31.05.1992 with full satisfaction and since then the plaintiff has been possessing and enjoying its interest by himself and his tenants. The plaintiff namely, Gazi Nur Mohammad died during pendency of Execution Case No. 72 of 1963 and his heirs namely, Hayet-Unness and others were substituted in the 1 case. The defendants refused and threw challenge over the right and status of the plaintiff on the suit land on 16.09.1994 on the basis of a decree in Title Suit No. 468 1982 and also threatened to dispossess. At that time, plaintiff filed Title Suit No.128 of 1994 for permanent injunction. But as it was in wrong forum, he finally withdrew the same. The Deputy Commissioner and others on behalf of the Government of Bangladesh filed another suit, bearing No. 34 of 1992, praying for declaring the alleged auction as well as the decree in Execution Case No.72 of 1963 as illegal, not binding upon and collusive, but that suit was ultimately dismissed. Since the defendants challenged the title of the plaintiff in the suit land referring their title in Suit No. 468 of 1982 and since the defendants claimed the suit land on 16.09.1994, the plaintiff in the circumstances, filed this suit for declaration of his title on the said land by dint of auction purchase and also declaring as not binding on plaintiff the judgment and decree dated 29.06.1986, passed by the Subordinate Judge, Chandpur in Title Appeal No. 71 of 1985, arising out of Title Suit No. 468 of 1982.

3. The case of the defendant No. 1, in short, is that the total area of land in Khatian No. 242 is 12 decimals containing .05 decimals in Plot No. 93 and .07 decimals in Plot No. 931/969 owned azad possessed by Shamkanto Das and Nibaran Chandra Das, in 8 status each, as Rayeti interest. Shamkanto Das sold his portion to one Suresh Chandra Chakraborti. Accordingly, S. A. Khatian was published in their names. The defendant No.1 took lease of .02 decimals of land including shops thereon in Plot No.931 and that Suresh Chandra Chakraborti left the country and went to India and the defendant No.1 took lease of the his property from the Sub-Divisional Officer, vide V. P Case No.8/82-83 and paying tent thereof from 1373 B. S. to 1380 B. S. at the rate of Tk400/- per year and from 1381 B.S. to 1389 B.S. at the rate of Tk.800/- per year. The defendant No.1 also has been paying U.P. Tax and doing business procuring license and setting electric meter thereto. The defendant No. 1 has been threatened by Nurul Islam, Abdul Bepari and Kasim Patari on 30.11.1982 and in order to resist them he filed Title Suit No.486 of 1982 for permanent injunction and during pendency of the suit, the defendant No. 1 was dispossessed from the land. So, he prayed for mandatory injunction. The suit was dismissed, whereupon an appeal was preferred and the same was allowed. Thereafter, the defendant of the suit filed a Civil Revision case before the High Court Division which was discharged. The plaintiff did not file any case for execution of decree, bearing number 72 of 1963 and no auction took place and that all are paper transactions, plaintiff has no right, interest, in the suit land. The plaintiff filed this suit falsely and that the suit is liable to be dismissed.

4. The defendant Nos.5 and 6, on behalf of the Government stated in their written statement that the Suit land measuring an area of .05 acres in Plot 93 under S. A. Khatian No. 229 of Mouza 18 Dasdi under Police Station and District-Chandpur and I .06 acres in Plot No. 931/969 is vested property and that .02 acres of land of plot No. 931 and .03 acres of Plot No. 931/969 i.e. in total .05 acres of land has been leased out to defendant No.1 vide Lease Case Nos. 8/82-83 and 3/81-82 and 21/82. Since the lease property is under possession and control of the Government, the case of the plaintiff should be dismissed.

5. Trial Court upon hearing the parties dismissed   the suit by his judgment and decree dated 02.03.2000. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree, the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No.41 of 2000 before the Teamed District Judge, Chandpur, which was heard by the learned Lawyers Additional District Judge, Chandpur, who allowed the same vide judgment and decree dated 31.03.2004. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment an decree dated 3.03.2004, the petitioner moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.1074 of 2004 and obtained Rule. The learned Judges of the High Court Division upon hearing the parties discharged the Rule without any order as to costs along with the connected Rule being Civil Rule No.928(R) of 2005 regarding status-quo and Civil Rule No.17(R) of 2006 vacating status-quo Hence this civil petition for leave t appeal.

6. Mr. Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing for the petitioner, submits that the impugned judgment and order dated 14.03.2007 passed by the High Court Division are had in law and fact and that the learned Judges of the High Court Division based their findings on surmise, conjecture and on extraneous circumstances for which the said findings are liable to be struck do He further submits that the High Court Division committed a grave error of law occasioning failure of justice in not appreciating that the trial Court after considering the facts and materials on record, found that the schedule of the auction purchase land as per Bainama vide exhibit-6 dated 26.01.1992 does not tally or is not identical with the suit land as mentioned in the schedule of the plaintiff and the identity of the suit land having not been established by local inspection, the s cannot be decreed and accordingly dismissed the suit and that on the other hand the appellate Court, though found that the Khatian No. 931 in the Bainama was wrong but held that the boundary of the auction purchase land was property given in the Bainama overtaking the fact that only the north and south boundary have been mentioned; that all sides have not been mentioned in the said Bainama and that the learned appellate Court below committed an error of law in allowing the appeal. His further submission is that the High Court Division miserably failed to take into consideration that the learned Appellate Court committed an error of law in holding that vide decree in Title Suit No. 3245 of 1958 (relating to non-suit land) the plaintiff established his title in the suit land and that the vested property an having been started much after 16.01.1962 after withdrawal of emergency there is no ground for treating the suit land as vested property overlooking the fact that the plaintiff also claim the suit land by auction purchase vide Bainama Ext.6 dated 26.01.1992 which relates to the land of Khatian No. 931 of 18 Deshdi Mouza but not relating to the suit land which is the land of C. S. Khatian No. 242 and S. A. Khatian No. 229 of the said Mouza and 0t that till today the said Bainama has also not been corrected if there is any mistake as alleged by the plaintiff.

7. We-have heard the learned Advocate-on-Record for the petitioner and perused the impugned judgment of the High Court Division and also other materials available on record.

<u>8. The learned Judges of the High Court Division found in the instant case, though there is some variations in plot and khatian but there is boundary in the Bainama which prove that the suit land is identical with the auction purchase land and both the Courts below upon appreciation of evidence on record came to the finding that the land in suit is not vested property, the revisional Court cannot interfere with the said concurrent findings of fact.</u>

9. The teamed Judges of the High Court Division having passed the impugned judgment and order on proper consideration of the evidence of the materials on record, this Division does not feel inclined to interfere with the same as the same does not suffer from any illegality or infirmity. Hence this petition for leave to appeal is thus dismissed having no merit.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 697 of 2007
lawyer:
Mahbubey Alam Senior Advocate, instructed by Chowdhury Md. Zahangir, Advocate-on-Record.  ------ For the Petitioner
