case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 25.01.2007 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.3380 of 2000).
full_judgment:
Md. Tafazzul Islam J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 25.1.2007 of the High Court Division passed in Civil Revision No. 3380 of 2000 discharging the Rule obtained challenging the judgment and order dated 30.6.2000 of the learned Additional District Judge, Second Court, Jhenidah, in Title Appeal No.125 of 1999 affirming those of dated 25.8.1999 of the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Jhenidah in Title Suit No.62 of 1988 decreeing the suit.

<u>2. Facts, in brief, are that the respondent No. 1, as plaintiff, filed the above suit seeking declaration of his title in the land as described Ka schedule of the plaint and also recovery of possession of the land described in schedule Kha of the plaint on the averments that .21 acres of land of Plot No. 243 described in Ka schedule belonged to Nayeb Ali who transferred the same to Rahim Sheikh by kabala dated 8.2.1939 and after the death of Rahim Sheikh his son Mahtab Sheikh became owner of the same and then Mahtab Sheikh, in 14th Chaitra 1346 settled the same in favour of Hemat Ali, the father of the plaintiff. Nayeb Ali by Patta dated 4.8.1938 and then Tezarat and Alekjan by Patta dated 8.2.1939 also settled Kha schedule land to Rahim Sheikh and after his death Mahtab became owner of the same and he by a registered kabuliyat dated 28.5.48 settled the same in favour of his son Hemat Ali who then gifted the .21 acres of land of Plot No. 243, that is Ka schedule, to the plaintiff and by kabala dated 23.1.1957 also transferred .17 acres of land of Plot No. 254 from Kha schedule land to the plaintiff and then on 15th Magh 1383 B.S, the plaintiff, for the first time, came to know that. 17 acre of land of Plot No. 254, that is Kha schedule land, has been wrongly recorded in the name of Rajab Ali and then he filed Title Suit No. 256 of 1973 against them and since they failed to appear the above suit was decreed exparte and that regarding .21 acres of land of Plot No. 243, which is Ka schedule land, the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 69 of 1976 but in view of a compromise which was made to the effect that plaintiff will possess Ka schedule land and Rahela Khatoon, who installed the defendant/petitioner in the suit land as her bargadar, will possess Kha schedule land, the plaintiff, in good faith, withdrew the above suit but no deed of exchange was then executed to the above effect and on the other the defendant, on 25.3.1986, dispossessed the plaintiff from Kha schedule land by erecting a house therein; subsequently after series of shalish the defendant handed over the Ka schedule of land to the plaintiff wherein he is living with his family and that the defendants, having denied his title in the suit land, he had to file the suit.</u>

3. The defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the material facts and contending that Rahim Sheikh, while owning and possessing both Ka and Kha schedule land, died leaving behind Mahatab Sheikh who, in the year 1346 B.S, orally settled the same in favour of Barkatullah, who then by Patta dated 16.7.1952 transferred his interest in the said land in favour of Yousuf Ali Biswas who in turn, by registered sale deed dated 19 Kartik 1362 B.S, transferred the same to Rajeb Ali Kazi and Maksed All Kazi who then by a registered deed of sale dated 3.10.73 transferred the same to Hasina Khatun and then Hasina Khatun by registered deed of sale dated 27.2.1976 transferred the same to Rahela Khatun who is possessing the same through defendant No.1, her bargadar and that Rahela Khatun by an agreement transfer schedules Ka and Kha land to the defendant No.1 and also one Latifur Rahman, her relation, but having not executed the sale deed the defendant No.1 and said Latifur Rahman filed a suit for specific performance of contract and obtained sale deed through court on 23.5.1990; subsequently the defendant No.1 after possessing the suit land from more than 12 years, in terms of an argument for sale and on accepting Tk.24,000.00, handed over possession of the same to Mujibur Rahman  and since then said Mujibur Rahman is possessing the suit land and Mujibur Rahman is a bonafide purchaser for value and that in the meantime a miscellaneous case has been filed praying for setting aside the decree obtained by the petitioner against Rahela Khatoon.

4. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, after hearing decreed the suit. On appeal, the learned Additional District Judge, after hearing, dismissed the appeal. The defendant then moved the High Court Division and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No.3380 of 2000 and the High Court Division, after hearing, discharged the Rule.

5. We have heard the learned counsel of the petitioner, and perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and also other connected papers.

<u>6. As it appears the trial Court decreed the suit holding that the plaintiff claimed his title on the basis of deed of settlement dated 28.5.1948 which was registered prior to the registered kabuliyat dated 7.6.48 produced by the defendant and further the title of the plaintiff has already been declared in Title Suit No. 265 of 1976 and though the defendant claimed that Title Suit No. 295 of 1996 challenging the decree passed in Title Suit. No. 265 of 1976 but yet did not get any relief therein and further the evidence on record also show that the plaintiff was given possession in Kha schedule land but thereafter the plaintiff was dispossessed from a portion thereof and the trial Court further held that -নালিশী জমি হইতে বেদখল সম্পর্কে বাদী দাবী করেন যে, বিবাদী পক্ষ গত ২৫-০৩-৮৬ইং তারিখে ঘর তুলিয়া এবং গত ২৬-০২-৮৮ইং তারিখে পুকুর খননের মাধ্যমে খ তপশীল জমি হইতে বাদীকে বেদখল করে। বাদী আরো দাবী করেন যে, অত্র মোকাদ্দম একতরফা সূত্র ডিসমিস হইলে আপীল দায়ের হয় এবং উক্ত সময়ে বিবাদী পক্ষ বাদীর আবাদী কলা, বেগুন, তিল, খেজুর গাছ কাটিয়া গত ২০-১১-৯০ ইং তারিখে কয়েকটি ঘর তুলিয়া বাদীকে বেদখল দেয়। বেদখল সম্পর্কে বাদী পক্ষের সাক্ষীদের সাক্ষ্য পর্যালোচনা করিয়া দেখা যায় যে, তাহারা বেদখলের সুনির্দিষ্ট দিন তারিখের উল্লেখ করে নাই। তবে আনুমানিক সময় কালে উল্লেখ করিয়াছেন। এছাড়া তাহাদের জেরা বক্তব্যে কতিপয় গড়মিল সাক্ষীগণও পরীলক্ষীত হয়। অনুরুপভাবে বিবাদীপক্ষের সাক্ষীগণও নালিশী জমিতে বিবাদীপক্ষের স্বত্বেও ভিত্তি নাই মর্মে নির্দিষ্ট তারিখ প্রমাণে আসা বাঞ্চনীয় ছিল, কিন্তু তাহা আসে নাই। আবার বৈধ স্বত্ব না থাকায় বৈধ দখল দাবী পরে করারও কোন অবকাশ নাই। বাদী পক্ষের বেদখলের নিদিষ্ট দিন তারিখ প্রমাণে না আসিলেও বাদী তদ্বীয় দাবীকৃত সময় কালের মধ্যেই বিবাদী পক্ষ কর্তৃক বেআইনী ভাবে বেদখল মর্মে বিবেচিত হয়। and further the appellate Court dismissed the appeal holding সংক্ষেপে যেটুকু পাওয়া গেল তাহা হইল এই যে, ইতি মধ্যে এখতিয়ার বান আদালত কর্তৃক বাদীর স্বত্বাধিকার নিশ্চিত হইয়াছে। এখন দ্রষ্টব্য যে, বাদী বিবাদীগণ কর্তৃক বেদখল হইল করে। জড়ুন মন্ডল দাবী করিয়াছেন যে, উক্ত মোকাদ্দমায় ডিক্রী হইবার পর সুকৌশলে প্রথমে ১নং বিবাদী অতঃপর ৫নং বিবাদী জোর পূর্বক ২৬-৮৮ইং তাহাকে বেদখল করিয়াছে। এখানে বলা বোধ করি অপ্রাসাংগিক হইবে না যে, প্রদর্শনী ৮ চিহ্নিত ১০-০৩-৮৬ইং ডিক্রীর তারিখে বাদীর দখল ছিল ইহা প্রমাণিত। বিবাদ বলেন যে, এখন বাদীর দখল নাই। পরে বিশ্বাস যোগ্য যে, ১০-০৩-৮৬ইং তারিখে তাহাকে বেদখল করা হইয়াছে দৃষ্টতঃ এই হিসাব সরল অংকের মত।</u>

7. সাক্ষীগণের ভাষ্যে পূণঃ পর্যালোচনা তথা প্রদর্শনী চিহ্নিত কাগজাদী বিশ্লেষণ স্পষ্ট প্রতীয়মান হয় যে, বাদীর পূর্বাপর দাবী যেমন ইতিমধ্যে নিশ্চিত হইয়াছে তখন পি, ডব্লিউ-৪ বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালতে তাহা পরিষ্কার করিয়া দিয়াছে। প্রসঙ্গগত আরও উল্লেখ্য যে, বর্ণিত বেদখলের তারিখ হইতে ১২ বৎসরের মধ্যে মূল মোকাদ্দমা দায়ের করা হইয়াছে এবং হেমাতুল্লাহর আর কোন ওয়ারিশ পিতা কর্তৃক পুত্র জুড়ুন মন্ডলকে নালিশী জমি মৌখিক দান এবং কবুলিয়ত মূলে বন্দোবস্ত সম্পর্কে কোন দাবী উথ্যাপন করিতেছেন না। ফলে পারিপাশ্বিক অবস্থা হিসাবে এইগুলি বাদীকে সমর্থন করে। অতি সংক্ষেপে আরও উল্লেখ্য যে, রাহেলা খাতুনের নিকট হইতে বিবাদী যখন জমি বাবদ রাহেলা খাতুনের বিরুদ্ধে ২৬৫/৮৬ নং দেওয়ানী মোকদ্দমা চলিতেছিল। সুতরাং মোকদ্দমা চলাকালে রাহেলা খাতুন কর্তৃক জমি হস্তান্তর সম্পর্কে বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত পারিত। দোষে বারিত মর্মে যে, অভিমত ব্যক্ত করিয়াছেন উহা প্রকৃত অর্থে আইনের সঠিক প্রয়োগ করিয়াছে।

<u>8. It appears that the High Court Division on a meticulous examination of the judgment of the trial Court as well as lower appellate Court and also considering evidence on record held that the lower appellate Court after discussing the evidence, both oral and documentary, elaborately and after proper assessment of evidence on record came to the finding that the plaintiff had been able to prove his right title and possession in the suit land and further the concurrent finding of facts should not be disturbed unless it is manifestly perverse and some are of the view that there being no illegality or infirmity in the above decision no interference is called for.</u>

9. The petition is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1846 of 2012
lawyer:
Shaheed Alam, Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner
Farooque Hossain, Advocate instructed by Abul Quasem, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondents
parties:
Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation and another ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Amena Khatun and another ------ Respondents
case_source: From the Judgment and order dated 29.02.2012 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1129 of 2004
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana, J. Delay in filing this Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal be condoned.

2. This Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal, at the instance of Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation, is directed against the judgment and order dated 29.02.2012 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1129 of 2004.

<u>3. The facts relevant for disposal of this Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal are that the present respondent No. 1 filed the above mentioned Civil Revision No. 1129 of 2004 before the High Court Division calling in question the order dated 24.02.2004 passed by the learned District Judge, Tangail in Money Execution Case No. 9 of 2000 rejecting the objection of the judgment-debtor (the respondent No. 1 herein) against the execution of ex-parte decree dated 28.10.1999 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 26 of 1998 for realization of loan of the House Building Finance Corporation. Rule was issued in that civil revision. During pendency of that rule, on 29.02.2012, the judgment-debtor-petitioner filed an application praying for disposal of that rule stating that she had already paid the loan amount. The High Court Division, in allowing that application, made some observations to the effect that according to section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation cannot claim any amount more than 3 times of the principal loan amount and as such since the House Building Finance Corporation took Tk. 28,87,000/- from the judgment-debtor-petitioner, which was more than 3 times of the amount taken as loan by the judgment-debtor-petitioner, House Building Finance Corporation would have to return the excess amount which, the High Court Division calculated as Tk. 4,48,000/-. The High Court Division disposed of the rule with a direction to the House Building Finance Corporation to return that excess money to the petitioner within 2 weeks from the date of receipt of that order.</u>

4. Being aggrieved by this order of the High Court Division Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation has filed this Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal.

5. We have heard Mr. Shaheed Alam, the learned Advocate for the leave-petitioners-who has admitted that the House Building Finance Corporation has already got the entire decreetal amount amounting to 28,87,000/- from the judgment-debtor-petitioner-respondent and now there is no amount due to him and that the House Building Finance Corporation has issued a certificate also to that effect. The leaned Advocate, however, has mode submissions that the observation of the High Court Division that section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is applicable in this case and as such the judgment-debtor-petitioner is entitled to get back the amount which is in excess of 3 times Limes of the principal loan amount-is wrong inasmuch as the House Building Finance Corporation filed the above mentioned Miscellaneous Case No. 26 of 1998 as per Article 27 of the House Building Finance Corporation Order, 1973 (P.O. 7 of 1973) for realization of loan along with interest accrued thereon in the court of the learned District Judge, Tangail and the learned District Judge, Tangail also disposed of that case as per that P.O. 7 of 1973 and in that case there was no scope for application of section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. The learned Advocate has argued that the observations of the High Court Division to the effect that according to section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 the judgment-debtor-petitioner is entitled to get back the excess amount is erroneous and illegal and the direction also made by the High Court Division to the House Building Finance Corporation to return 4,48,000/- to the judgment-debtor-petitioner has been illegal.

<u>6. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate and gone through the impugned order of the High Court Division. We find substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the leave-petitioners. The observations made by the High Court Division in the impugned order to the effect that section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is applicable in this case and as such the decree-holder House Building Finance Corporation cannot get any amount more than 3 times of the principal loan amount from the judgment-debtor-petitioner is wrong. The present case for realization of loan was not filed before the Artha Rin Adalat as per provision of the Arthat Rin Adalat Ain 2003, rather it was filed before the learned District Judge as per Article 27 of the House Building Finance Corporation Order, 1973 (P.O. 7 of 1973) . In this case there is no scope for application of section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003.</u>

7. In the circumstances the direction to the House Building Finance Corporation to refund Tk. 4,48,000/- to the judgment-debtor-petitioner (the present respondent No. 1) made by the High Court Division in the Impugned judgment be expunged.

8. This Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal is thus disposed of with the above observation and modification of the impugned judgment and order.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1373 of 2008
lawyer:
Md. Awlad Ali, Senior Advocate instructed by Nurul Islam Bhuiya, Advocate-on-Record.   ------ For the Petitioners: 
For the Respondents  ------ Not represented.
parties:
Surendra Mohan Bandayapadhya being dead his heirs- 1( 2) Paritosh Kumar Bandayapadhya and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Lalit Mohan Das being dead his heirs-1(a) Ratan Kumar Das and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 23.04.2008 passed by the high Court Division in Second Appeal No. 435 of 1971.)
full_judgment:
Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman J: This leave petition of the plaintiff petitioner is for leave to appeal against the judgment and decree dated 23.042008 passed in Second Appeal No.435 of 1971 by a Single Bench of the High Court Division dismissing this appeal affirming the judgment and decree dated 26.5.1969 passed in title Appeal No.256 of 1968 by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Faridpur, allowing the appeal dismissing the suit being Title Suit No.66 of 1967, decreed by the Munsif, 1st Court, Madaripur, vide judgment and decree dated 29.8.1968.

<u>2. The predecessor of the petitioners filed Title Suit No.66 of 1967 in the Court of Additional Munsif, Madaripur, for declaration of his hostile title in the suit land and for further declaration that the rent roll as prepared in respect of the suit land has been wrongly prepared and also prayed for confirmation of possession. The plaintiff Nos.1 and 2 claimed title by way of inheritance and the plaintiff Nos. 3 and 4 claimed title on the basis of auction sale in a revenue case and that the defendant Nos.3 and 4 some time after partition of India left East Pakistan for West Bengal surrendering the suit tenancy against redemption of arrear rent, in favour of the plaintiff Nos.1 and 2 in the month of Agrahayan 1350 B.S. and they never came back to this country and that the plaintiff Nos.1 and 2 took khas possession of the land and have been enjoying usufructs therefrom. The contesting defendants manufactured and forged an antedated amalnama in respect of the suit land showing the defendant Nos.3 and 4 as grantor and the defendant No.1 as recipient and by false personification massaged to file Rent Suit No.1250 of 1955 in the name of the defendant Nos.3 and 4 and obtained a sole decree by practicing fraud upon the Court and taking advantage of the said decree, the defendant filed a Criminal Case against the plaintiff in the Court of S.D.O. Madaripur under Section 379 of the Penal Code alleging theft and taking away of crops from the suit land by the plaintiff, wherein the plaintiff was convicted and punished but on appeal was acquitted and that the appellate Court on scrutiny of the documents doubted the amalnama and observed that the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 were not residing in the country after 1354 B.S. and thus found the amalnama of 1358 B.S., allegedly executed by defendant Nos.3 and 4, to be a forged document.</u>

3. The plaintiff filed Title Suit No.66 of 1967 for declaration of title and confirmation of possession in the suit land. The suit was decreed against the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 on contest and exparte against the rest. The trial Court found title and possession of the plaintiff in the suit land observing that the plaintiff became tenant under the Government by operation of law after acquisition of the rent receiving interest. The trial Court disbelieved the witnesses of the defendants since they made contradictory statements as to possession of the suit land and found the witnesses adduced by the plaintiff to corroborate the story of possession of the plaintiff in the suit land. The defendants claim of possession on the basis of settlement was disbelieved as the documents produced in support of the settlement i.e. the Amalnama and the rent receipts were found to be forged documents (Exhibits-B, B-1) and that the tenancy in respect of the suit land was surrendered in favour of the plaintiff landlord by the defendant Nos.3 and 4 before their leaving Pakistan and thus the plaintiffs were found in khas possession of the suit land and it was also found that from the deposition of the D.W. that the defendant Nos.3-4 left for West Bengal and before their departure they surrendered the tenancy in favour of the plaintiff landlords in the month of Agrahayan, 1350 B.S., which correspondence to 1943 A.D. The trial Court framed 5 issues in arriving at its decision and found that the suit was not barred by limitation and the suit was not hit by the Ordinance 1 of 1964 and that the plaintiff proved their right, title, interest, and possession in the suit land and the plaintiff succeeded to prove title and possession in the suit land and thus entitled to get a decree as prayed for. Being aggrieved the defendant Nos.1 and 2 preferred Title Appeal No.256 of. 1968 in the Court of District Judge, Faridpur, which was heard and disposed of by the learned Subordinate Judge, Faridpur, by judgment and decree dated 26.05.1969 allowing the appeal holding, amongst others, that the suit was hopelessly time barred and the defendants were in possession of the suit land since Falgoon 1358 B.S. and that the learned Munsif acted illegally in discarding the depositions of D.Ws.2-6 and 8 summarily on the plea of some discrepancies found in the depositions of defendant Nos.1 and 7, and the appellate. Court further held that the depositions of P.Ws. 2- 6 in proving the plaintiff's possession of the suit land, though appear to be of independent witnesses, but their evidence cannot get preference to those of D.Ws. since supported by documentary evidence, marked Exhibit-B series and F, and thereby the appellate Court believed the possession of the defendant in the suit land. The appellate Court also believed the amalnama and thereby relying on the said amalnama found the  title of the defendant in the suit land.

<u>4. The High Court Division, being moved by the plaintiff in Second Appeal No.435 of 1971, on consideration of the materials on record and on detailed discussion on the depositions of plaintiff's witnesses dismissed the appeal observing that the definite case of the plaintiff was that the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 surrendered the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs on Agrahayan 1350 B.S. and the P.Ws. 2-4 have clearly supported the surrender of the suit land by the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 in favour of the plaintiff in the year 1350 B.S. and that it has been stated that the defendant Nos. 3-4 left Pakistan soon after independence. The year 1350 B.S. correspondence to 1944 A.D. whereas Pakistan got independence in 1947. The plaintiffs case of possession and title on the basis of such surrender has no standing in the eye of law. The learned Advocate appearing for the leave petitioner failed to explain the story of surrender of the suit land in favour of the plaintiff by the defendant Nos.3 and 4 in the year 1350 B.S. as against the statement that the defendant Nos.3 and 4 left this country soon after creation of Pakistan and never returned back and thus we do not find any point to interfere with the decision of the High Court Division inasmuch as the said judgment and decree appears to have been passed on proper discussion made and consideration on the facts and evidences on record.</u>

5. Accordingly, the application for leave to appeal is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1619 of 2008
lawyer:
Nikhilesh Dutta Senior Advocate instructed by Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner 
Respondents ----- Not represented
parties:
Mansur Ali ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Mst. Monowara Begum and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
B. K. Das J: This petition for leave to appeal has been filed against the judgment and order dated 08.05.2008 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4481 of 1999 discharging the rule upon affirming the judgment and decree dated 7.9.1999 passed by the then Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Narayanganj in Title Appeal No. 73 of 1996 up holding those dated 20.6.1996 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sonargaon, Narayanganj in Title Suit No. 42 of 1995 granting a decree in favour of the plaintiffs. 

2. The petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 3 of 1989 in the court of the Assistant Judge, Sonargoan, Narayanganj praying for declaration that the decree obtained by defendant Nos. 1-3 in Title Suit No. 3 of 1989 is void, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiffs. 

3. The plaintiffs case, in short, is that .65 decimals of land in plot No. 127 of Jyanedra Narayan Chowdhury was inherited by his only son Akshay Kumar who by a Hukumnama gave settlement to Ilias Bepari in 1356 and he died leaving 3 sons, 3 daughter and a widow; that Mohammad Ali by amicable arrangement got the suit land who died leaving the plaintiffs as heirs who rented the suit land to C.I.A brick field in 1979; that the defendants No. 1-3 with a view to grab the suit land brought' Title Suit No. 3 of 1989 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sonargaon, without implicating the heirs of Ilias Bepari stating that Akhoy by Hukumnama gave settlement of the suit and to Asgar Ali who on 13.12.1937 sold to Momin Ali," Monsur Ali and Abedin Ali stating that in the deed Khatian, plot number and the quantum of land was wrongly written; that Akshay never gave settlement of the suit land to Asgar Ali and as such the defendant have no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land; that the plaintiffs learnt about the above facts from the written statement of the defendants in their Title Suit No. 70 of 1992 and as such they were constrained to bring the suit. 

4. That the defendants No. 1/2 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying the material allegations contending, inter alia, that the original owner Akshay Kumar gave settlement of the suit land to Asgor Ali who while owning and possessing the suit land sold to defendant with delivery of possession on 13.12.37 and that defendant No. 3 exchanged his share of 22 decimals of land with his elder brother Mohan Chan; that the defendant having learnt of the wrong writing of plots Number, Khatian and quantum of land in the sale deed brought Title Suit No. 3 of 1989 for correction which is a valid decree. That the plaintiff also brought Title Suit No. 70 of 1992 for permanent injunction against one Nuruddin, subsequent purchase of suit land from them which was dis-missed on contest and being frustrated thereof brought the instant suit; that the defendants are owning and possessing the suit land; that defendant No. 1 sold 21 decimals out of 65 decimals of suit plot to Dr. Mr. Malek and others and purchased .22 decimals with his brother Mohar Chan. That the plaintiffs have no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land. Hence the suit in liable to be dismissed. 

5. The learned Assistant Judge though found that the plaintiff failed to produce anything to show settlement of the suit land but found possession of the plaintiff because of the record of the right and by judgment and decree dated 20.6.1996 decreed the suit. 

6. Against the said judgment and decree the defendant preferred Title Appeal No. 73 of 1996 before the learned District Judge, Narayanganj. The learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 1st Court, Narayanganj affirmed the decision of the trial court by judgment and decree dated 7.9.99. 

7. Being satisfied with the decree, of the lower appellate court the defendant being the petitioner obtained a rule being Civil Revision No. 4481 of 1999 before the High Court Division and a Single Bench of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order dated 08.05.2008 discharged the rule. 

8. Being aggrieved thereby the defendant as petitioners filed the present petition for leave to appeal before the Appellate Division.  

9. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the High Court Division misdirected itself with the finding of the courts below with regard to plaintiffs title and possession in the suit land which are not supported by the evidence on record and thus the impugned decision needs to be set aside. The learned Advocate further submits that the High Court Division was wrong in failing to hold that in Title Suit No. 70 of 1992 the defendants (petitioners herein) were not parties and thus they were not bound by the said decree and accordingly the plaintiffs acquired no title in the suit land. The learned Advocate then submits that the High Court Division acted illegally in failing to notice that the courts below illegally found possession in favour of the plaintiffs upon misreading of evidence and thereby the impugned decision suffers from illegality and infirmity. 

10. We have heard the learned counsel and perused the impugned judgment and all other connected papers. It appears that the suit land admittedly belonged to Ganenra Narayan Bondhapaddhay who died leaving behind a son Akshay Kumar. From finding of the courts below it appears that Akshay Kumar granted settlement of the suit land by a Hukumnama with one Ilias Bepari and the S.A. khatian was prepared in the name of Ilias Bepari and there is no evidence that any step was ever taken to get the record-of-right corrected and the courts below concurrently held that the plaintiffs could prove his right title and possession in the suit land and this finding was rightly maintained by the High Court Division and we do not find any error in the decisions of the courts below holding that the plaintiffs have acquired title to the suit land. It further appears that though the S.A. khatian was prepared in the name of Ilias Bepari, in the suit filed by the defendants for permanent injunction the said Ilias Bepari or his heirs were not impleaded and the High Court Division correctly found that the decree obtained in the said suit by the defendant is not binding on the plaintiffs and the plaintiffs title has not been defeated by the said decree. Having considered the pleadings of the parties and the findings of the courts below we are of the view that the judgment of the High Court Division does not suffer from any illegality or infirmity and we do not find any substance in any of the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner. 

11. Accordingly this petition for leave to appeal is dismissed. 

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 533 of 2009
lawyer:
A. J. Mohammad Ali, Senior Advocate, instructed by Haridas Paul, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioners 
For the Respondents ----- Not Represented
parties:
Md. Sona Ullah being dead his legal heirs: Md. Akbar Ali and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Most. Morium Bewa and others ----- Respondents
case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 28.10.2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1642 of 2003)
full_judgment:
S. K. Sinha J:-This leave petition at the instance of the defendants is directed against the judgment and order dated 28th October, 2008 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1642 of 2003 making the rule absolute. 

2. Respondent Nos.1-11 instituted Title Suit No. 45 of 1992 in the Court of Senior, Assistant Judge, Sadar, Rangpur against the petitioners for declaration that the ex-parte decree passed in Other lass Suit No. 199 of1984 by the Assistant Judge, Kawnia Upazila is not binding upon them and recovery of khas possession of the lands described in the schedule 'Ka' to the plaint. 

3. Short fact of the plaint case are that 'Kha' schedule lands measuring an area of 2.39 acres belonged to Doyel Bibi, Jasiron Bibi, Bariron Bibi and Bacchani Bibi. They paid rents to the ex-landlord and subsequently surrendered the said lands to the landlord Tasiruddin Sarkar. The landlord possessed the said lands for some time and subsequently he granted pattan to Ambaruddin and Genda Mahmud. Thereafter said tenants sold the same to Saiab Uddin, Sharof Uddin and Wahab Uddin by deed dated 13th January, 1940. The R.S. Record was prepared in the name of Sharof Uddin and Wahab Uddin, the predecessors of the defendant Nos. 2 to 13. During the war of liberation, all the title deeds were destroyed. The defendant Nos. 2-12 sold the 'Ka schedule lands out of 'Kha' schedule to the plaintiffs by different deeds. On 10th September, 1990, the plaintiffs came to know for the first time from the defendant No.1 that he obtained an ex-parte decree in Other Class Suit No. 139 of 1984. On the basis of such information, they procured a copy of the judgment in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 86 of 1987 arose out of the suit and came to know about the suit. The said ex-parte decree is not binding upon the plaintiffs. The defendant No. 1 has no right, title and interest in the suit lands who forcefully dispossessed the plaintiffs from the 'Ka' schedule lands on 2nd January, 1991. Hence the suit. 

4. The defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing a written statement. His case in short is that one Jallad Sheikh owned of the suit lands, who died-levering behind wife Doyel Bibi and three daughters, namely Jasrion, Basiron and Bacchoni. The C.S. record was also prepared in their names. Subsequently Doyel Bibi died leaving daughter's daughter Tepri Bibi. Jasiron died leaving son, the defendant No. 1 and Basiron died leaving two sons Baher and Meher. Defendant No. 1 purchased .80 acres of land from Tepri Bibi and .80 acres of land from Baher and Meher by deeds dated 5th June, 1983 and 9th June, 1983, respectively. In this way' the defendant No. 1 is the exclusive owner by way of inheritance and purchase. The R.S. Khatian having been wrongly pre-pared in the names of Sharof Uddin and Wahab Uddin, the defendant No. 1 instituted Other Class Suit No. 419 of 1983 in the First Court of Munsif, Rangpur which was renumbered as Other Class Suit No. 139 of 1984. The suit was decreed ex-pane on 22nd July, 1987. The defendants of that suit thereupon instituted Miscellaneous Case No. 3 of 1987 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex-parte decree. On being are unsuccessful, they preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 86 of 1987 which was also dismissed for default on 15th May, 1990. During the pendency of the said cases, the plaintiffs procured the collusive deeds from the judgment debtors. The plaintiffs have no right, title and interest in the suit lands. 

5. The learned Assistant-Judge on consideration of the evidence on record by judgment and order dated 10th September, 1994, decreed the suit in part holding that the plaintiffs came to Court with defective title but their predecessors had possession in the suit lands, that the plaintiffs have been in possession thereon, that the documentary evidence of the plaintiffs are more stronger than that of the defendant, that the defendant dispossessed the plaintiffs during the pendency of the suit and erected a house subsequently and that the plaintiff are entitled to get a decree as prayed for. With these findings, the learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit in respect of 1.2212 acres of land and directed the defendant No. 1 to vacate possession therefrom. 

6. On appeal by the defendant No. 1 being Other Class Suit No. 206 of 1994 from the aforesaid judgment and decree, the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Rangpur, who heard the said appeal 4k- by judgment and order dated 28th November,2002, reversed the findings of the trial Court and dismissed the suit. The court of appeal below held that the plain-tiffs failed to prove their claim that the tenants Doyel Bibi and others surrendered possession in favour of the plaintiffs' landlord Tasiruddin Sarkar, that Jasiron Bibi being the heir of C.S. recorded tenant inherited the suit lands from whom the defendant No. 1 accrued title in the suit lands. The court of appeal below further held that the plaintiffs also failed to prove that Ambar and Ganda took pattan of the suit lands from the ex-landlord and there-fore, the plaintiffs acquired no title on the basis of purchase from Sharof Uddin and Wahab Uddin and that the plaintiffs purchased the suit land during pendency of the cases and litigations arose out of other Class Suit No. 139 of 1984. 

7. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and order, the plaintiffs moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1642 of 2003. A single Bench of the High Court Division by judgment and order dated 28th October, 2008, made the rule absolute and restored those of the trial court by setting aside the judgment and order of the court of appeal below. The learned Judge of the High Court Division Observed that the decree passed in Other Class Suit No. 139 of 1984 is not binding upon the plaintiffs, that the defendant No. 1 did not make any statement that he constructed homestead on the suit lands prior to the institution of the suit, that though. Ws. 3,4 and 6 failed to mention the date of dispossession but that the evidence of EWs.1-5 and.7 are more stronger than those of the defendant No. l. 

8. Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners contended that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division erred in law interfering with the findings of fact arrived at by the court of appeal below and therefore, the learned Judge of the High. Court Division exceeded its jurisdiction while exercising revisional power. The learned counsel further contended that the learned Single Bench erred in law in failing to consider that the plaintiffs have purchased the suit lands during the pendency of Miscellaneous Appeal No. 86 of 1987 arose out of Other Class Suit No. 139 of 1984 and therefore, their claim of title on the basis of deeds are hit by the principles lispendens. The learned Counsel further contended that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division erred in law in holding that the evidence regarding the possession and dispossession adduced by the plaintiffs are more stronger than those of the defendant, in failing to consider that the court of appeal below on a proper appreciation of the evidence on record found the defendant's possession which finding being based on assessment of the' evidence on record is binding upon the High Court Division and that the learned Judge of the High Court Division failed to notice that in a suit for declaration under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, the Court can not pass a decree for recovery of khas possession 'under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act. 

9. We find substance in the contentions of the learned Counsel for the petitioners. Leave is, therefore, granted on the additional grounds as follows: 
"I. For that out of the 7 plaintiffs seeking declaration that the ex-parte decree in Title Suit No. 139 of 1984 is not binding upon them in respect of 1.2212 acres of the snit land, the trial court gave declaration only in favour of plaintiff No. 3 to the extent of 25 acres of the suit land, which was reversed by the Appellate Court but the High Court Division without adverting to the said findings of the courts below simply held that the plaintiffs have been able to prove the fact that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 139 of 1984 is not binding upon them though the courts below clearly held that except for the case of plaintiff No. 3, the other plaintiffs purchases were hit by lispendens and this has resulted an 'error in the decision of the case on its merits. 
II. For that the Appellate Court having reversed the findings of the trial court on the question of possession and dispossession, made on treating the case as one under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, the High Court Division erred in holding "In view of the above I am constrained to hold that the evidence of possession and dispossession as adduced by the P.Ws.175, P.W.7 are more stronger and reliable than that of the defendant. Their evidences inspired me to hold that the plaintiffs were in possession in the suit land and were dispossessed during the pendency of the suit". Because appraisal of evidence and disturbing the finding of fact in revisional jurisdiction is only permissible when the finding of fact is based on misreading or non-consideration of evidence by the court of fact.
III. For that having regard to the frame of the suit, namely, ex-parte decree is not binding upon the plaintiffs and for eviction and the trial court haying granted the declaration only in respect of plaintiff No. 3 but not granted by the Appellate Court on the ground that the transfers were hit by lispendense, the' High Court Division erred in ignoring the same on the plea of dispossession having occurred during the pendency of the suit overlooking that the transfers in favour of the plaintiffs were hit by lispendence." 

10. Security of Tk.1000/- is to be deposited within one month. 

11. Preparation of paper book is dispensed with as prayed for. 

12. The petitioner is permitted to add additional grounds. 

13. The order of status-quo granted earlier by this court shall continue till disposal of the appeal. 

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Apple No. 1707 of 2008
lawyer:
Syed Humayun Kabir Khadem, Advocate instructed by Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-On-Record ------ For the Petitioner 
For the Respondent ------ None represented.
parties:
Abdul Khaleque Khalasi ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Saburun Nessa and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 15.05.2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.1610 of 2004)
full_judgment:
Md. Muzammel Hossain J.: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 15.05.2008 passed by a Single Bench of. the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1610 of 2004 discharging the Rule and affirming the judgment and decree dated 05.01.2004 passed by the learned Jolla District Judge, 1st Court, Madaripur in Title Appeal No. 31 of 1996 reversing the judgment and decree dated 25.11.1995 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Shibchar, Upazilla Court, District-Madaripur in Title Suit No. 107 of 1993 decreeing the suit

2. The facts of the case, in short, are that the petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 79 of 1987 in the Court of Munsif, Madaripur which was subsequently on transfer to Shibchar renumbered as Title Suit No. 107 of 1993 in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Shibchar for having a decree for declaration of title and confirmation of possession of the suit property.

3. The plaintiffs case is that the property mentioned in schedule No. 1 of the plaint measuring 1.44 acres of land in plot Nos. 308 and 309 under Khatian No. 314 of Mouza Ghotmajhi, Police Station and District-Madaripur belonged to Monai Khalashi, Tamijuddin Khalashi and Wafazuddin Khalashi in equal share, Azimuddin, Kazem Uddin and Kalai Khalashi owned 1 annas 15 gandas 2 kara 13 til of Plot Nos. 1791, 1792, 1784, 1775, 1876 under C.S. Khatian No. 676 of Monza Ghotmajhi. Imanuddin Khalashi and Sonamuddin Khalashi sons of Monai Khalashi each owned and possessed 2 annas 13 gandas 1 kara 1 kranti and Ofazuddin Khalashi owned 5 minas 6 gandas 2 karas 2 kranties in the said khatian and accordingly R.S. Khatian was correctly prepared. Monai Khalashi was owner-in-possession of 5 annas 6 gandas 2 karas 2 kranties share in plot Nos. 308 and 309 under C.S. Khatian No. 314 and thus he was owner in possession of 45 decimals. Monai Khalashi died before the R.S. record of rights leaving behind two sons, namely, Imanuddin Khalashi and Sonamuddin Khalashi. Thereafter Imanuddin died leaving behind only son Abdul Khaleque Khalashi (Plaintiff-Petitioner) and thereafter Sonamuddin Khalashi died without any issue and wife of Sonamuddin died during Sonamuddin's life time. Thus Imanuddin's only son Abdul Khaleque Khalashi inherited owned and possessed 1.04 acres of land as described in the schedules of the plaint. Imanuddin Khalashi during his life time never sold any land to anybody. He died leaving behind his one Minor son the plaintiff, and the plaintiff’s Uncle Sonamuddin Khalashi reared plaintiff and died without any issue excepting his only heir the plaintiff-petitioner. At the time of last S.A. record taking advantage of the plaintiff’s minority, the defendant Nos.  1 to 3 and the predecessor of defendant No. 4 collusively created incorrect and false S.A. record in the names of those persons though they had no title and possession over the suit land. On the other hand plaintiff has been possessing the suit land for a long time by constructing home and hearth and enjoying the same exclusively. But in the month of Falgun, 1393 B.S. the said defendants disclosed about the wrong S.A. record and threatened the plaintiff to enter into the suit land. Hence the plaintiff filed the instant suit.

4. The respondent Nos. 1-5 as defendant Nos. 2, 4(Ka)-4(Gha) contested the suit by filing written statement admitting ownership in C.S. Khatian No. 314 and R.S. Khatian No. 676 and alleged that on the death of Sonamuddin Khalashi without any issue his brother Imanuddin inherited his share and remained owner-in-possession of the same but contesting defendants claimed that the father of the plaintiff Imanuddin Khalashi executed a safkabla deed on 05.02.1944 and registered the same on 17.02.1944 in favour of Azimuddin Khalashi Azimuddin Khalishi and Jangu Sarder became owner-in-possession of lands of R.S. Khatian Nos. 676 and 680 and Imanuddin Khalashi predecessor of the plaintiffs sold his share in those khatians in favour of Azimuddin Khalashi and thus Imanuddin had no title and possession in those lands.

5. It has been alleged that lands of RS. Khatian No. 676 described in the 2nd schedule of the plaint were the lands of C.S. Khatian No. 313 Monai. Khalashi, Taimuzuddin Khalashi and Ofazuddin Khalashi were equal owners-in-possession in those lands and Monai Khalashi died leaving 2 sons Imanuddin and Sonamuddin. Sonamuddin died without any wife and issues and his only brother Imanuddin obtained his share. Thus Imanuddin inherited the entire 1/3rd share of Monai Khalashi alias Monizuddin sold his share from the schedule No. 1 and his share described in schedule No. 2 of the plaint in the name of Sakina Khatun, Abdul Jasim, Abdul Kader and Abdul Waned on the basis of saf-kabala deed dated 31.01.1944 but Azimuddin Khalashi predecessor of these defendants obtained the same by a pre-emption decree dated 26.02.1944 in Miscellaneous Case No. 34 of 1944 under Section-26F of the B.T. Act. Thereafter Azimuddin Khalashi purchased .08 decimals of land from C.S. Plot No. 103 of schedule No. 2 and Imanuddin's shard, from schedule No. 1 by a saf kabla deed executed on 05.02.1944 and registered the same on 17.02.1944. After such sale Imanuddin Khalashi had no right, title and possession in the schedule 1 and 2 lands and plaintiff has no title and possession in its schedules 1 and 2 lands. Moreover in the suit jama plaintiff has no title and possession in any other lands on the other hand defendants Nos. 4 (ka) to 4(Gha) have been possessing the lands purchased. That Tamuzuddin Khalashi died leaving 3 sons namely, Kamez, Kalai and Azimuddin as heris Kamez Khalashi died leaving behind his only son namely Malek Khalashi, Kalai Khalashi died leaving behind his only son Halan Khalashi. Azimuddin Khalashi gifted his share in favour of his daughter defendant No. 2 and wife Samartaban Bibi by a registered deed of gift. Samartaban Bibi transferred gifted share to her daughter defendant No.  1 It has been alleged that Azimuddin's heirs defendant Nos. 1 and 2 have been owning and possessing .04 decimals of land and defendant Nos. 4(ka) to 4(gha) have been possessing the lands purchased by them. Ofazuddin died after R.S. record of right leaving behind his 2 daughters namely Faljari Bibi and Malu Bibi and one sister. Fajjari Bibi and sister sold their shares to Azimuddin and Jangu Sarder. Malu Bibi died leaving behind her son, daughter and husband who sold some lands to the plaintiff Abdul Khaleque Khalashi. It has been alleged that Imanuddin sold his entire share and suit land was recorded in the name of the defendants and as such the suit of the plaintiff is liable to be dismissed.

6. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, Shibchar, Upazilla Court, District-Madaripur by the judgment and decree dated 25.11.1995 in Title Suit No. 107 of 1993 decreed the suit on finding that the plaintiffs title and possession in the suit land. Contesting defendant-respondent preferred Title Appeal No. 31 of 1996 which was allowed by the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, Madaripur, 1st Court, Madaripur by the judgment and decree dated 10.03.1998 setting aside those passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge. The plaintiff-petitioner being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree 10.03.1998 passed by the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, Madaripur, 1st Court; Madaripur filed Civil Revision No. 1212 of 1999 before the High Court Division. A Single Bench of the High Court Division after hearing sent back the case on remand for hearing by the court of appeal below according to law. The Court of Appeal below again allowed the appeal by the judgment and decree dated 05.01.2004. Again the plaintiff-petitioner against the judgment and decree dated 05.01.2004 preferred Civil Revision No. 1610 of 2004 before the High Court Division and a Single Bench of the High Court Division after hearing the parties and on perusal of the materials on record was pleased to discharge the Rule by the judgment and decree dated 15.05.2008 1 affirming those passed by the Court of appeal below.

7. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree plaintiff petitioner preferred this Civil Petition for leave to Appeal before this Hon'ble Court.

<u>8. Mr. Syed Humayun Kabir Khadem, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the High Court Division committed an error of law in not considering both documentary and oral evidence of the witnesses on record and passed the impugned judgment and decree which suffers from misreading and non-consideration of the evidence and materials on record. He then submits that the High Court Division failed to consider that the plaintiff-petitioner has inherited the property from his father and he has a dwelling house over the part of the same and possess the remaining portion of the property by cultivation and that the evidence of P.Ws.3, 4 and 5 and that of P. W. 1 as to the possession and very much corroborative of each other. He finally submits that the plaintiffs suit was a suit for declaration of title and confirmation of possession so the revisional court ought to have considered the question of possession independently and while doing so the trial court found that there is a graveyard of the plaintiffs father over the suit property and also the homestead of the plaintiff and as such the transfer of property as claimed by the defendants respondents was not proved and the High Court Division failed to consider this aspect of the matter and as such the same is liable to be set aside.</u>

9. We have heard the learned Advocate for the petitioner and perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and also other materials available on record.

10. In view of the above, we find substance in the submissions of the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner. Accordingly, leave is granted on consideration of ground Nos. 1-4.

11. Security of Tk. 1,000/- is to be deposited within one months.

12. The petitioner is permitted to prepare paper books out of court in accordance with law.

13. Parties are at liberty to mention the appeal for expeditious hearing.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1103 of 2009
lawyer:
Md. Nur Hossain Chowdhury, Advocate instructed by, Syed Mahbubar Rahman Advocate-on-Record ----- For the petitioners

full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique J.:- This Petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 5.2.2009 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 5164 of 2000 discharging the Rule affirming the judgment and decree dated 18.6.2000 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Sylhet in Title Appeal No. 205 of 1989 confirming those dated 27.9.1989 passed by the Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Sadar, Sylhet in Title Suit No. 61 of 1987.

2. The facts, in brief, for disposal of the petition are that the petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 196 of 1981 in the Court of the then Munsif, Sylhet, Sadar (which was subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 61 of 1987 in the Additional Court of Assistant Judge, Sylhet, Sadar) for declaration of their jot right in the suit. land and for further deceleration that the order of resumption of the suit land in Resumption Case No. 138 of 1965 by Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Sylhet vide his Memd No. 11438/1(4) dated 23.12.1965 and subsequently in Miscellaneous Case No. 8/79-80 by the Revenue Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet are illegal, void and those are not binding upon the plaintiffs. Their case is that the suit land originally belonged to Proshanna Kumar Dey, Basanta Kumar Dey and Aswani Kumar Dey, They settled the same to plaintiff No. 1 and Monaullah, the predecessor in interest of plaintiffs Nos. 2-4 by executing a Hukumnama on 7.10.46. They paid rent to the Landlord and received "farogs" and took over possession of the suit land. Receiving notice in Miscellaneous Case No. 8/79-80 they came to know about the Resumption Case No. 138 of 1965. The defendant No. 4 disclosed that he had taken settlement of the suit land from defendant No. 2. Thus the cause of action of the suit arose.

3. The defendant Nos. 1 and 4 contested the suit by filing two separate sets of written statements denying all the materials allegations contending, inter alia, that the Government took over possession of the suit land in Resumption Case No. 138 of 1965 and thereafter settled the same to Badrul Hossain, the defendant No. 4 and Suruj Ali. They have been possessing the suit land. The defendant No. 4 in his written statement contended that the suit land is the khas land of the Government and the Government settled the same to him by registering bilateral lease deed. He paid consideration and has been possessing the same. Earlier the plaintiff No. 4 filed an application addressing the then Sub-divisional Officer, Sylhet for getting lease of the suit land which was rejected on 21-8-68. Mona Ullah predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiff Nos. 2-4 and Lunee Bibi (petitioner No. la), wife of plaintiff No. 1 Instituted Title Suit No. 12 of 1969, This defendant No. 4 appeared in the said suit and filed written statement. The said suit was dis-missed for default on 21.3.73. The plaintiffs have no title and possession in the suit land. So the suit should be dismissed.

4. The Trial Court disbelieved the Hukumnama, the instrument of settlement and possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land. The plaintiffs preferred appeal and the Appellate Court also disbelieved the Hukumnama of the plaintiffs but found their possession in the suit land. Then the plaintiffs filed revisional application in the High Court Division and obtained Rule. The High Court Division, ultimately, discharged the Rule.

<u>5. Mr. Md. Nur Hossain Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that the plaintiffs petitioners have been possessing the suit land about 67 years thereby acquired title in the suit land by way of adverse possession. But the plaintiffs did not claim the title in the suit land on the basis of adverse possession rather they claimed their right in the suit jote on the basis of Hukumnama dated 7.10.46 which has been disbelieved by the courts of facts. Adverse possession ripens into a title only if the said possession is hostile, uninterrupted and without any protest by the true owners. A plea of adverse possession, being based on facts, which have to be raised to that effect, is not necessarily a legal plea. The doctrine of adverse possession would arise only when the party has set up his own adverse title, disclaiming the title of the owner and establishing that he remained exclusively in possession to the knowledge of the owner, hostile to his title and the owner had acquiesced to the same. The elements to get a decree of title on adverse possession have not been established in the instant case.</u>

6. Mr. Chowdhury relied upon section 110 of the Evidence Act. But the presumption that possession follows title is not absolute. It is a discretionary one depending upon the circumstances of each particular case.

7. Mr. Chowdhury next submits that the respondents have failed to prove their claim of acquisition of possession of the suit land in resumption case. It is true that the courts below held that the contesting defendants have failed to prove the order of resumption but such failure on the part of the defendants would not establish the title of the plaintiffs in the suit land on the basis of their Hukumnama. The plaintiffs are not entitled to get decree depending upon the weakness of the case of defendants.

8. Earlier Lance Bibi, wife of plaintiff No. 1 and Mona Ullah, predecessor in interest of the plaintiff Nos. 2-4 instituted Title Suit No. 12 of 1969 in respect of the land recorded in Plot No. 172, 179, 183 which was dismissed for default in 1973. After about 8 years of dismissal of the said suit, the plaintiffs instituted the present suit claiming that they got the suit land on the basis of a Hukumnama of 1946. The courts below did not commit any error in taking notice of the aforesaid fact while taking decision of dismissal of the suit.

9. Since the courts of facts disbelieved the story of settlement, which has been affirmed by the revisional court, we do not find anything to interfere with the matter.

10. Accordingly, the petition is dismissed.

End.
